Sports.title: Man Utd launch major US court blitz against websites accused of flogging fake shirts and merchandise
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER United have launched a major US court blitz against websites accused of flogging fake club shirts and merchandise.

The Premier League giants have filed at least 11 lawsuits this year, including three in the space of six days last month, against online traders allegedly selling counterfeit United gear.



It comes after The Sun revealed the Red Devils are the Premier League club worst hit by fake football shirts, with 38.4 per cent of shirts checked using an authentication app suspected of being counterfeit.

US court records show the club filed three of its latest cases on August 26, 28 and 31 in Chicago.



The most recent accuses a group of unidentified businesses and traders of trademark infringement.

In one case launched in February, United targeted 24 online sellers with names including yami_jerseys, jersey.factory44 and soccer.shirt.foot.



The club secured an asset freeze before later winning default judgments against almost all of them.

Another action in June initially targeted 57 alleged counterfeit sellers.

City of London Police revealed in July that more than 220,000 fake football shirts worth an estimated £18.5million had been taken off the market since January.

United say fake shirts do not undergo the same quality checks as official merchandise.



Experts have also raised concerns about potentially unsafe dyes and other substances in counterfeit clothing.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick ‘can’t wait’ for apology from refs chief Howard Webb after Man City’s controversial winner vs Man Utd
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED coach Michael Carrick sarcastically said he “can’t wait” for an apology from referees’ chief Howard Webb after 10-man City’s controversial derby winner.

Erling Haaland’s 60th-minute goal was initially disallowed but then given following a VAR check after the Norwegian was deemed to be onside from Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross.



The offside Enzo Fernandez dived towards the ball before it reached Haaland but the Premier League Match Centre confirmed that the goal stood as Fernandez did not connect with the ball.

ProRef has since contacted Man Utd to ‘acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement’ – and will launch an investigation into the incident



Carrick was bewildered by the decision to let Haaland’s eventual winner stand, consigning United to as bad a start in the Premier League as last season.

The 45-year-old also questioned the line drawn to determine that Haaland was played onside by Patrick Dorgu.

Carrick said: “The explanation I got was he wasn’t interfering with play. So I just don’t get it. I really don’t get it.

“I can’t understand how they’re trying to help referees and putting so many layers behind them with so many people, so many bodies, so many screens, and so many whatever offices they are to try and come up with the right decisions.

“If that’s how the rules are interpreted, that you’re not interfering with play because you’ve thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Licha (Martinez) has to react from.

“On top of that, the line was a bit dubious where they drew the line to start with. It’s worrying if that’s really how the game’s seen by those who are officiating it.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Carrick did not speak any further with on-pitch referee Michael Oliver and indicated he had little appetite to contact Professional Game Referees, previously known as Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL).

“I don’t know how you can (get in touch with them). I don’t know where you go.

“I don’t really know how you go and get another explanation on that one, I have to say.”



When someone suggested United could receive an apology, Carrick replied: “Yeah, that’d be great, that. Yeah, I can’t wait for that one.

“I think we all understand what that rule means, and it’s pretty obvious.

“So I don’t think there’s a tweaking of the rules where sometimes there’s a little change. Maybe you only hear it in the meetings and as a general public, you’re a bit confused sometimes.

“But for that, I think it’s as obvious as it gets.”

United struggled to create a standout opportunity until the fifth minute of added time after Haaland’s poached strike.



Carrick admitted the manner of the breakthrough affected the United players: “It’s part of the game but it did have a major impact, for sure.”

Sports.title: VAR got Erling Haaland goal wrong and should not have got involved in Manchester derby controversy, says ex-ref Halsey
Sports.content:
THE “subjective” nature of VAR once again dominated a big game in the Premier League in the Manchester derby, and former Premier League referee Mark Halsey has weighed in on the debate.

Erling Haaland‘s strike on the hour was the difference between the teams, but there were a couple of grey areas surrounding the goal.



The Norwegian initially thought he was denied by the offside flag, but replays with the lines drawn from the technology actually showed Patrick Dorgu‘s foot played him on.

However, Enzo Fernandez launched himself at Josko Gvardiol‘s cross trying a diving header.



The Argentine was clearly offside, hence the flga. But he was not adjudged to have been interfering with play as he didn’t touch the ball – which was the view from VAR.

In the end, the goal stood and City held on for all three points to ensure they, alongside Arsenal, started the season with maximum points and four wins from four.



Halsey said: “We saw more controversy in the Manchester derby. Haaland has put Manchester City 1-0 up only for the assistant referee to rule the goal out as offside.

“Now when we look at it, Haaland is not offside but Fernandez is offside. When the ball comes across, he’s in an offside position.

“Being in an offside position is not an offence in itself. It only becomes an offside offence if the player involved becomes involved in active play by interfering with an opponent or making a deliberate play to play the ball.

“In my opinion, Fernandez does that. And I believe that the assistant referee was correct in flagging Fernandez as offside.

“Obviously all goals are checked. VAR have looked at it, and they have decided that the goal is onside.

“In my opinion, it’s subjective to whether you feel Fernandez is making a deliberate play for the ball, or becoming involved in an active play and interfering with defenders.

“If that’s the case, the subjectivity – VAR – should not have got involved. They should have stuck with the on-field decision of offside, which I believe was the correct call.”



It would have been hard to envisage City winning in the 23rd minute when Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes – something Halsey believes Michael Oliver got right.

Sports.title: Three things we learned from Man Utd defeat to Man City as transfer issue becomes clear and Fernandes theatrics fail
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED played 70 minutes against ten men in their derby clash with Man City and still left with nothing.

A Phil Foden red card isn’t even the main talking point after the Manchester derby – it’s should Erling Haaland‘s winning goal have stood?



Even so, United played better while they were battling 11 men than they did subsequently against ten.

So what did we learn about Michael Carrick‘s troops following the derby defeat? With four points from their first four games, the landscape is changing fast at Old Trafford.



Wrong on the right

After starting all 38 last season, it took three Premier League games for left back Luke Shaw to drop like a fly this season. That cost United, with left back liability Patrick Dorgu responsible for turning attack into defence for City’s goal.

United have issues on the other side, too. Diogo Dalot was unconvincing at both ends, failing to get on the end of a perceptive pass from Bruno Fernandes and then twice playing his side into trouble with daft attempted lay-offs.

Dalot was also lazily flagged offside. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha immediately gave him a ticking off.

This was Dalot’s 250th appearance for United and he is into his ninth season at the club. United have not had a right back who has come close to elite since Gary Neville before his crippling ankle injury in March 2007. That is almost 20 years.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Noussair Mazraoui has not convinced in either of his starts against Hull City and Sabah and Dalot wears the number two for a reason. This was additional evidence that United have to be in the market for a high-class right back, as well as a left back, next summer.



Carrick reactive, not proactive

United supporters sang Benjamin Sesko’s name to the old Andy Cole song as the Slovenian striker warmed up in the second half. Michael Carrick ignored them.

Sesko did not emerge for another 19 minutes. By that time, Erling Haaland had put City ahead and United were now chasing an equaliser, rather than an opener.



It was clear in the first half United again lacked a focal point. Carrick had 22 minutes to assess them against ten men before the interval and decided to continue with a strikerless side.

There was an argument to introduce Sesko at the interval. By abiding by the ‘give it 15 minutes’ cliche, Carrick left it too late. Haaland prodded in on the hour.

Fernandes’ theatrics fail to work in his favour

Officials almost always give Bruno Fernandes short shrift when he is on the deck but it was impossible to ignore Phil Foden’s reaction.

Fernandes was snide to boot Foden a couple of times while he was prone, provoking a rash flick and milking it.



However much Foden hurt Fernandes, it was a red card offence from Foden. Yet it did not galvanise Fernandes, whose ball-striking was sloppy and his influence not as profound as in the corresponding fixture last season.

If anything, Fernandes seemed slightly fazed by the stick City fans gave him as he prepared to take a corner in front of them. He hit the first man.

Fernandes eventually snapped in the 78th minute when he barracked the dozy Dorgu for an errant pass.

Sports.title: VAR debate is a happy distraction for Michael Carrick who is to blame for ineffectual Man Utd
Sports.content:
VAR debate is a happy distraction for Michael Carrick who is to blame for ineffectual Man Utd

Phil Foden's early red card threw Manchester United's game plan out of the window and Michael Carrick was unable to adapt, with Manchester City the better side despite being down to 10 men

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is yet to prove his credentials (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

If you're going to lose a derby it's best to have a big controversial refereeing decision to rage against.

‌



"It's a staggering decision," Michael Carrick said after Manchester United were beaten by 10-man Manchester City at Old Trafford. "I can't understand it once I seen it then the explanation almost makes it worse."

‌



If you're going to lose a derby it's even better to have a solid point when raging against a controversial decision. There are plenty of people who would agree with the United manager's take on the VAR process around awarding Erling Haaland's winning goal.

‌



It was the perfect smokescreen for Carrick. Sky Sports' post-match analysis was completely dominated by the offside law and its interpretation, with Micah Richards and Gary Neville baffled.

That's not to say that no-one noticed United's shortcomings. Those leaving Old Trafford on Sunday evening will rightly have been as frustrated by the Haaland goal as their side's inability to make the most of their numerical advantage.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

But in the social media age, we are hyper-focused on officiating and all too happy to declare conspiracies. And that means, for the majority, the discussion in the coming days will be around VAR, as is often the case.

That suits Carrick down to the ground. Because he doesn't want the spotlight on him after an absolute stinker of a performance in one of the biggest games of the season.

‌



Phil Foden's red card in the 23rd minute was a nightmare for United, because it threw their game plan out of the window and piled on the pressure in front of the home crowd. Now the expectancy was for United to dominate, to lay siege to the City goal and win the derby.

View 3 Images Phil Foden's red card put pressure on Manchester United and they couldn't handle it (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Instead, City looked like the much better side. Elliot Anderson had struggled to cover both Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha in the space in front of the City defence. But the red card and Enzo Maresca's shift to a 4-4-1 formation minimised that space and forced United out wide.

‌



Carrick had no answers. He tried two things. The first was blatantly obvious: bringing on Benjamin Sesko to provide a focal point up front. The second was desperate: introducing Joshua Zirzkee - a player United tried hard to sell two weeks ago - for Marcus Rashford.

United hit the post twice, through a Rashford free-kick and a curling Kobbie Mainoo attempt. Bryan Mbeumo shot straight at Gianluigi Donnarumma in added time. That was pretty much the grand total of their attacking moments, with their three shots on target amounting to 0.95 xG, less than City's 0.99 xG.

The United hierarchy had little option but to hand Carrick the full-time job in the summer after he built up a head of steam in the second half of the season and the other candidates failed to materialise. But this game showed what Carrick's detractors argued: that he struggles to deliver when it really matters.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester United failed to make the most of their numerical advantage (Image: Joe Prior/Visionhaus via Getty Images)

It's one thing guiding United to wins in the wake of the miserable Ruben Amorim era, when they've been knocked out of both cup competitions and don't have any European fixtures. It's another when you're no longer the interim boss and there are games every three days.

What makes this defeat even more worrying is that United were able to coast to a 4-0 win over Champions League debutants Sabah on Thursday in a glorified training match. There will be tougher tests to come when a Premier League game follows a genuinely competitive Champions League tie.

Article continues below

Carrick is clearly liked by his players. He's erudite and hard-working. But what he hasn't shown is an ability to deal with pressure in the biggest games.

The City defeat leaves United with four points from four games. They've conceded twice against Hull, Ipswich and Everton. Yes, the Haaland goal was questionable, but the biggest question mark is over their manager.

Sports.content:

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes' lamentable behaviour in Phil Foden incident not befitting of Man Utd captain
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes' lamentable behaviour in Phil Foden incident not befitting of Man Utd captain

Bruno Fernandes' behaviour made sure Phil Foden was shown the red card in the Manchester derby and the United captain then went missing against City's 10 men

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes got Phil Foden sent off (Image: Shaun Brooks/Getty Images)

First things first, you will be glad to know Bruno Fernandes is okay. Bet you were worried for him after that vicious attack from well-known hard man Phil Foden.

‌



“More of a flick or a gesture,” said Wayne Rooney. And he was absolutely spot-on. It was an angry gesture, for sure. But that was about it.

‌



Fernandes writhed around as though he had been kung fu-kicked in the solar plexus, and Michael Oliver bought it in the same way that Foden had bought it. Both fell for Fernandes's dark arts.

‌



“He’s helped his team-mates there,” remarked Gary Neville, unsurprisingly. Fernandes might have helped his team-mates but it was still a pretty lousy cameo. Yes, he is probably in a majority when it comes to trying to get opponents sent off, but it is still lousy.

This is the Professional Footballers Association Player of the Year, don’t forget. Is it too idealistic to think a player might NOT try to get a fellow pro dismissed and banned? Yes, of course it is. Enzo Fernandez was at it later, trying to get Kobbie Mainoo and Harry Maguire in trouble. It is lamentable. But it is not going to change.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Anyway, the harsh dismissal of Foden was the sole responsibility of Oliver, who, incidentally, had more touches of the ball than Haaland. Matthew Donohue, the VAR, was never going to tell the country’s top-billed referee that he might have got it wrong.

But he was happy to award a goal to Erling Haaland after lengthy deliberation. There will be many out there who still don’t understand how Haaland’s effort - well-taken, to be fair - was allowed to stand.

Surely Enzo Fernandez, clearly offside, was having an impact on proceedings. So, although they will be losing Foden for three games, City cannot really complain about the officiating.

‌



View 3 Images Phil Foden was shocked by the red card (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

And as it happened, the red card ended up having a negligible effect on proceedings. If anything, it might have somehow made United a touch complacent - although considering their current status, that would be hard to believe.

This was a real setback for Michael Carrick. He was unable to galvanise his team, unable to elicit any sort of reaction after Haaland’s controversial goal.

‌



Yes, Bryan Mbeumo might have rescued a point in added time but the lack of imagination in United ranks was startling.

Perhaps Fernandes felt guilty for getting Foden sent off. It was a brutal result for Carrick and United, who are already eight points behind City and Arsenal.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick's honeymoon is over (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



At the final whistle, Carrick turned to shake Enzo Maresca’s hand, only to find the City manager was already in front of the visiting fans, punching the air. And the Italian did not seem to seek out Carrick after he had gone around each of his City players, giving them a hug.

It left the United boss to walk from the field on his own, head down, no doubt considering the possible injustice of the winner but, more than likely, considering the size of the challenge ahead.

That golden interim period seems a long, long time ago.

Sports.title: Gary Neville calls for officials to apologise over Erling Haaland's controversial goal
Sports.content:
Gary Neville calls for officials to apologise over Erling Haaland's controversial goal

Erling Haaland's goal settled the Manchester Derby for City, but Enzo Fernandez's offside position and attempt to play the ball has sparked fury among the pundits

View 2 Images Gary Neville was confused by the decision (Image: The Gary Neville Podcast/Sky Sports)

Gary Neville has demanded an apology from Pro Ref after Erling Haaland's controversial goal settled the Manchester Derby. Haaland's strike saw 10-man Manchester City win at Old Trafford in a match shrouded in debate.

‌



The City striker's goal from Josko Gvardiol's deflected cross was initially ruled out for offside before VAR overturned the on-field decision. Haaland was played onside by Patrick Dorgu, but Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position when the ball passed him and the City midfield made an attempt to head it in front of Lisandro Martinez.

‌



Explaining the decision, the Premier League Match Centre wrote: "VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

‌



Neville was confused by the call while on co-commentary duties for Sky Sports. "The officials will be nervous about this goal," Neville said. "When they look back on this, they will recognise they got this wrong.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"The question is does Fernandez, who is offside, stop Martinez getting the ball? He does."

‌



After hearing the explanation, he added: "They're the words that I think – emphatically – means we will see an apology from Pro Ref.

"There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off. It’s a really strange one. They’ll recognise they got that wrong."

Neville did concede that "Manchester City have been very good" but reiterated that there should be "a massive inquest into the goal which I think was wrongly given."

‌



View 2 Images Erling Haaland's goal was allowed to stand

The former Manchester United defender was far from the only pundit to question the decision. Wayne Rooney said on the BBC: "Surely it's offside. Martinez is impacted by Enzo's movement, and he is offside."

Replying to the Premier League Match Centre's explanation, Rio Ferdinand wrote on X: "Enzo Fernandez not played the ball?" He then shared a screengrab of Fernandez stretching to try and head the ball.

‌



Ferdinand then posted: "Martinez has to go defend the man nearest the goal whether he believes he’s offside or not. In split seconds, you make the decision. He goes to defend Fernandez - who then attempts to play the ball. Deluded from VAR!"

Ex-Manchester City defender Micah Richards said on Sky Sports: "I think it's been a bad day for referees, it's been a bad day for VAR. I think they got the Phil Foden decision wrong on 23 minutes and they got this decision wrong.

"How can you say that Enzo Fernandez is not challenging for the ball?! I've been in that situation as a defender and any slight movement can make the difference between going for the ball or not. Of course it affects it! I just think they've got it so wrong."

Sports.title: Fuming Lisandro Martinez hits out at 'injustice' after controversial Man Utd decision
Sports.content:
Fuming Lisandro Martinez hits out at 'injustice' after controversial Man Utd decision

The Manchester United defender made his feelings clear when addressing Erling Haaland's winning goal, which was allowed to stand after initially being flagged for offside

View Image Lisandro Martinez was visibly fuming after the game

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez hit out at what he called an 'injustice' after Erling Haaland's opener was initially ruled offside during the Manchester derby. Martinez was positioned between Enzo Fernandez and Haaland, but the Argentine launched himself toward the ball in an attempt to meet it with a diving header.

‌



Following a lengthy VAR review, it was determined that the Manchester City striker was onside and that Fernandez, despite standing in an offside position, had not played the ball, with Martinez defending behind him. Josko Gvardiol's shot deflected off Patrick Dorgu towards the back post, where the Norwegian finished smartly.

‌



A tweet from the Premier League Match Centre said: "#MUNMCI – 59’ VAR OVERTURN. VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

‌



Wayne Rooney slams Manchester derby VAR call as Man Utd left furious READ MORE :

The rules state that an opponent will be penalised for interfering with play if they clearly attempt to play a nearby ball in a way that impacts an opponent, or if they make an obvious action that affects an opponent's ability to play the ball.

However, Martinez did not agree with the decision to overturn the offside call.

"I think he was offside," the Argentine told Sky Sports post match. "What I can't understand is the rules, you know? He was there, I went to him because he was in front of me that's why Haaland was free but I want to be calm now, I want to control myself.

‌



"So hard because you lost the derby, three points at home. Every time they come to our club, they explain one hour, hour and a half with the rules then after five or six people doing this kind of mistake in the PL is unacceptable. You have the best players, best teams in the world and now we have to go home with this injustice.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"For sure, it's difficult. I have two players there and I was 50/50, had to take the first guy in front. Simple as that (if Enzo isn't there goes to Haaland), let's see what they have to say, let's see, I want to hear what their decision is. Based off what? I want to hear it."

‌



United head coach Michael Carrick also slammed the decision that cost them a 1-0 defeat to City. He said: "Confused, not even confused, we've put things in place to help referees' decisions, screens, referees in an office somewhere. It's more worrying about if that's the interpretation about football.

"If we've got people in place that are meant to understand a game of football or not interfering with play or impacting an attack, throwing your body at it with a defender next to him, it's really worrying for me. It's a staggering decision. I can't understand it once I seen it then the explanation makes it worse.

"The explanation that he's not interfering with play. Incredible. It's not going to change a season, it's a major impact on the game and it's a massive game. It's a long season ahead, we've got to get back to winning football matches, that's on us, that (decision) wasn't on us today."

‌



On Sky Sports commentary, Gary Neville was baffled as the still images suggested Haaland was behind the last defender. "I'm going to need the offside law explaining to me, it's lost me," he said.

"The question is does Enzo Fernandez put off Lisandro Martinez? I think he does because he sort of hesitates. I do think when they look back, they'll recognise they got it wrong," before adding: "Well VAR looked at this for a long, long time. They say Haaland's onside from Dorgu's foot, from where we were didn't look the case but Dorgu's foot is deeper."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho has his say on Michael Carrick's Man United job with 10-word verdict
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho has his say on Michael Carrick's Man United job with 10-word verdict

Jose Mourinho was recently asked about Michael Carrick and how he has been faring at the Special One's former club Manchester United

View 3 Images Jose Mourinho was ambushed by Martin Brundle during the Spanish GP grid walk (Image: Sky Sports)

Jose Mourinho heralded Michael Carrick for "doing well" as manager of Manchester United. The Special One offered his opinion while at the Spanish GP, not long after his Real Madrid side overcame Rayo Vallecano 4-1.

‌



Carrick is now the United manager, nearly eight years after the Reds sacked Mourinho. While United have endured an inconsistent start to the new campaign, Carrick's excellent impact last season saw him be handed the role full-time.

‌



Mourinho was asked to offer his thoughts on the Englishman, just before the Manchester derby between United and Manchester City kicked off. The former Chelsea boss had nothing but praise for the Englishman.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He said: "He's doing well Michael, doing well. I'm happy with that."

The Portuguese oversaw 144 fixtures as United's boss from May 2016 to December 2018. In that period, he steered the Reds to a Community Shield, Europa League and League Cup triumph.

‌



However, following a disappointing third season at Old Trafford, he was shown the door in favour of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Mourinho has since made his return to Real Madrid and earlier this year opened up about his spell in Manchester.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has experienced a mixed start to his first season as permanent Manchester United manager (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

The 63-year-old said: "My career at Manchester United, I know it well. I also know the reason why I ended up leaving.

‌



"But as I always do, or try to do, when I leave a club I close the door and then I do not make comments. I do not analyse externally what happened.

"A door closes and another one will open. That is what happened when I left. The history stayed there, the numbers stayed there, the three medals came home and that is it."

View 3 Images Jose Mourinho has started promisingly at Real Madrid (Image: Soccrates Images, Getty Images)

‌



For Carrick, United's opening to the 2026/27 season has proved testing. It began disastrously with a shock 2-0 away loss to Hull City, but they bounced back with a 5-2 home win over Ipswich Town.

They were seconds away from overcoming Everton at Hill Dickinson, but Ainsley Maitland-Niles' 96th minute thunderbolt secured a draw for David Moyes' side.

United got back to winning ways in the Champions League by beating Azerbaijani side 4-0 at Old Trafford. Meanwhile, Mourinho's side are second in La Liga, having won four and lost one of their opening five matches.

Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez left 'out' of Atletico Madrid squad as statement released on Arsenal transfer target

Julian Alvarez has been ruled out of Atletico Madrid's La Liga clash with Real Sociedad on Sunday amid links to Arsenal

View Image Julian Alvarez will miss Atletico Madrid's match against Real Sociedad through injury (Image: Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez has been omitted from Atletico Madrid's travelling squad as the La Liga side gear up for Sunday night's clash with Real Sociedad. The club moved quickly to stress that his absence is purely injury‑related, distancing it from any remaining tension after a long, Arsenal‑shadowed summer transfer saga.

‌



When announcing their squad for the 8pm kick‑off at the Reale Arena, Atleti confirmed via social media: "Julian will not travel to San Sebastian due to a muscle overload that led to his withdrawal from yesterday's training session. After conducting the relevant tests, the medical services have ruled out his participation in today's match."

‌



Transfer insider Fabrizio Romano had earlier reported: "Julian Alvarez, out for Atletico Madrid today and not even travelling with the squad."

‌



Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool READ MORE :

The news comes amid a turbulent return to La Liga for Alvarez, following a lengthy transfer saga that dragged on for the best part of two months, with both Barcelona and Arsenal circling. The Gunners made no secret of their desire to land the 26-year-old as a marquee signing, as they look to defend the Premier League title they won in May.

Barcelona had also thrown their hat into the ring for the Argentine, but Arsenal received a significant boost in their pursuit when Atleti flatly refused to sell Alvarez to their domestic rivals.

Despite their utmost efforts, Mikel Arteta and the Arsenal board fell short of securing a deal for the striker, with the club opting to begin the campaign with Kai Havertz shouldering the bulk of their attacking responsibilities.

‌



That outcome has ultimately worked in the club's favour, as they have made a flawless start to 2026/27, claiming wins in all four of their opening fixtures.

Sports.title: Wade ends 10-year European title drought with victory in Flanders
Sports.content:
James Wade ended a decade-long wait for a European Tour title as he beat Ross Smith 8-4 in the final of the Flanders Darts Trophy.

The 43-year-old, who last tasted continental glory at the European Darts Matchplay in Hamburg in 2016, produced a 95.50 average and five 180s in the final in Antwerp on Sunday evening.

Earlier in the day he'd beaten Damon Heta 7-4 in the semi-final, having whitewashed Danny Noppert 6-0 in the quarter-finals and edging Rob Cross 6-5 in the last 16.

"Some weeks it's good, sometimes it's bad. That's how it is for me," he said after claiming the £35,000 prize money.

"If it was good all the time, I'd smash them all to bits. We can't always select how we feel."

Wade played in the first European Tour final in Austria in 2012 and this win means he was victorious in the 150th event.

Smith, who won the Hungarian Darts Trophy two weeks ago, beat Gian van Veen, Ryan Joyce and Gerwyn Price in last-leg deciders earlier on Sunday.

"I rode my luck today and the players have let me off, but Wadey, doesn't let you off ever," Smith said.

"I admire him. I watch his game and I can only admire the guy.

"James thoroughly deserved the win today. He's just-he's absolutely class, isn't he?"

The European Tour returns at the Swiss Darts Trophy in Basel, Switzerland from October 9-11.

Sports.title: Awarding Man City's winner at Man Utd an error, admits refereeing body
Sports.content:
Refereeing body Pro Ref has admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford.

In a statement released just hours after Man City's win, Pro Ref revealed it had made contact with Man Utd to acknowledge an "error of judgment" and that the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner.

The striker's goal was initially disallowed for offside on the pitch before VAR overturned the decision.

The VAR officials deemed that Haaland was played onside by Man Utd defender Patrick Dorgu. However, Man City's Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position as he attempted to play the ball before it reached Haaland.

Despite not touching the ball, Fernandez's movement appeared to impact the defending of Man Utd's Lisandro Martinez before Haaland's back-post finish, which by the laws of the game should have led to the goal remaining disallowed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville slams VAR's decision to give Erling Haaland's goal in the Manchester derby

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville reacts to Manchester City's controversial winner against Manchester United

A Pro Ref spokesperson said: "Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal.

"The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland - that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

"In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

"Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place."

What is Pro Ref? Pro Ref (Professional Game Referees) is English football's refereeing body, which was formerly known as PGMO (Professional Game Match Officials) after a rebrand in the summer.

Ex-Premier League referee Howard Webb leads the body, which oversees the four men's top divisions, the National League, the WSL and the U21s Premier League 2.

What did the officials say?

Who were the match officials at Old Trafford? Referee: Michael Oliver

Assistants: Stuart Burt, Tim Wood

Fourth official: Paul Tierney

VAR: Matt Donohue

Assistant VAR: Blake Antrobus

In their post on X explaining why the goal was awarded, the Premier League Match Centre wrote: 'VAR checked the referee's call of no goal for offside - and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn't play the ball.'

That stress on Fernandez not playing the ball chimed with replays shown during the VAR review, in which the VAR officials apparently sought to detect whether or not the City midfielder played the ball.

However, the offside rule clearly stipulates that a player can be offside despite not playing the ball and can interfere with an opponent by:

preventing an opponent from playing or being able to play the ball by clearly obstructing the opponent's line of vision or

challenging an opponent for the ball or

clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent or

making an obvious action which clearly impacts on the ability of an opponent to play the ball

Neville predicted error admission

Speaking at the time of the goal on co-commentary, Sky Sports' Gary Neville believed the VAR officials were "wrong" to award Haaland's effort.

Pro Ref's statement, however, fell short of Neville's prediction that they would apologise.

The former Man Utd defender told Sky Sports: "We will see an apology from Pro Ref.

"There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off.

"It's a really strange one. They'll recognise they got that wrong."

Speaking on his podcast, Neville continued: "I think they are ignoring the rule.

"They are digging themselves a bigger hole [with the Match Centre statement]. I'm really surprised they put that out.

"They will have to retract that."

He told Sky Sports: "Every season the officials come to our club and spend an hour explaining the rules and they look so confident with that.

"Then after, five or six people [officials] doing this kind of mistake in the Premier League is unacceptable.

"We have to go home with this injustice."

Richards: 'Goal award was a nonsense'

Former Man City defender Micah Richards dismissed Match Centre's explanation that the goal was awarded because Fernandez didn't touch the ball as a "nonsense".

Asked whether Fernandez was clearly attempting to play the ball, Richards told Sky Sports: "One hundred per cent he is.

"I think it's been a bad day for referees and VAR.

"They got the Phil Foden decision wrong, and they got this decision wrong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United’s match against Manchester City in the Premier League

"How you can not say Enzo Fernandez is challenging for the ball - of course he is!

"I've been in that position as a defender where any slight movement can make the difference for going for the ball or not, so of course it affects him.

"I just think they've got it so wrong."

Roy Keane concluded: "Fernandez is interfering with play. Basically, United have been punished for holding a good line. When you are in that position, you are impacting the game. You're in the middle of the box, you're going for the ball.

"Their line is good. Fernandez is offside, and he goes to play the ball, so United are getting punished for good defending."

Sports.title: Nordqvist hits back at USA ‘dig’ over Solheim course set-up
Sports.content:
Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist was quick to shut down suggestions the Bernardus Golf course set-up had been tailored to suit the home team at the Solheim Cup.

Nordqvist's side completed a 15-13 victory over Team USA after prevailing in Sunday's singles in the Netherlands.

The scores were tied at 8-8 following the opening two days, but USA captain Angela Stanford felt her side had been at a disadvantage throughout the tournament due to the slowness of the greens.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sunday singles from the Solheim Cup

Stanford said at her post-tournament press conference: "Europe played well. I don't think we played bad. I think we just didn't make enough putts.

"And if you listen to everything I've ever said, Europeans always putt better. I don't know why. I still don't know why. I mean, I have a good idea, but I'm not going to say it right now.

"Apparently I didn't get to know the superintendent [grounds manager] as well as I should have."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team Europe started dancing and celebrating after their Solheim Cup win

When pressed further about whether she was referring to the green speeds being different to what she had been expecting, Stanford added: "Even when we showed up in July here, they were faster.

"And I don't think it had anything to do with the rain either. Now, saying that, it's my responsibility to get the team ready.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team USA's Nelly Korda appeared to tell a fan to 'have some class' after playing a shot on the 16th hole at Bernardus Golf

"This is the one thing I am kicking myself is that I just didn't keep pushing, you know, we got to figure out how to hit our putts a little bit harder, which is really difficult, to change the way you putt.

"So I'm a little frustrated with myself that I didn't drive that point home."

'We're in Europe in September'

Nordqvist was a little surprised by the apparent dig at the greens when it was put to her at her own press conference.

"We're in Europe and in September. We know how the weather can be," she said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist reacts to winning the Solheim Cup

"I'm not sure I believe a lot in setting up a way to fit Europe because these girls play the same golf courses week-in and week-out competing.

"We came here in July, it was a very hot and dry summer, so the course played a little bit different then.

"So if anything it was just really trying to manage firmness. But then it's obviously been raining a lot in the past couple weeks and then this week we saw a lot of rain.

"So if anything they were probably just playing a little bit softer than we all thought coming here. But that's obviously the weather, we can't control that."

Image: Anna Nordqvist proudly holds the trophy

Stanford: You don't want to take away those moments

The Americans were pictured celebrating on Saturday evening after Jennifer Kupcho had sunk two brilliant putts to snatch a late victory for the visitors and level the match at 8-8 rather than going into the final day trailing 9-7.

But Stanford dismissed suggestions they had reached an emotional high too early.

"That's kind of tricky because you don't ever want to take away from that moment," she said.

"The worst thing I could have done is go in there and be like, 'okay, y'all. Come off this high'. So you don't want to take away from those moments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Saturday fourballs from the Solheim Cup where Jennifer Kupcho's heroics levelled the contest for the USA

"We're never going to see anything like that again. I think they handled it very well.

"But I talked to Kupcho and everybody and they're like, 'yeah, we got good rest but, yeah, it did take a minute to come off because it was a pretty high high'."

What's next?

The Ladies European Tour heads to Spain next for La Sella Open, beginning Thursday and held at La Sella Golf Resort, while the LPGA Tour takes a week off before the Walmart N Arkansas Championship from September 25-27.

Sports.title: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.

Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.

However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of there [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

"A race should be won by the guy who can put in the best performance. Maybe you take a risk by running long in a stint and maybe you get a Safety Car and things can help because you know that's one of the big factors.

"But for everyone to get a VSC pit stop and for me to not, it's just.. unfair. But it's happened in the past. Others have won from it, I've probably won from it in the past. I just don't think many people have lost a race win over it. It's frustrating. I don't feel that's the way you should lose."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix

Race-winner Antonelli stated he "felt bad" for Norris and the McLaren driver feels everyone should have the opportunity to pit, should a VSC be called.

"We have spoke about it in the past in drivers' briefings saying they [race control] should leave it out for at least a lap, so it's equal for everyone," he continued.

"I was the only one that lost out and I lost out on about 20 seconds of race time and that's not how it should be."

Former F1 strategist Bernie Collins on the VSC rules Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins



“I don’t think the rule needs to change. The rule is there for safety.



“There’s always a question mark on people changing tyres under a red flag but the VSC and Safety Car is there for the safety of a driver who crashed or gone off track and the marshals on track.



“Kimi Antonelli has been one of the most unlucky people with VSCs and Safety Cars. Monaco he missed two Safety Cars, Austria as well.



“It’s come around. It hurt Norris this week and will benefit him at another point.”

McLaren chief executive Zak Brown told Sky Sports F1: "They [the VSCs] were cruel today twice!

"Lando was gone, the team did a great job and the VSC came out a couple of seconds after we went by and went away a couple of seconds before we could pit.

"Nothing we could have done. Great to hear Lando's radio message to 'shrug it off'. That was our race by 20 or 25 seconds. He was dominant, he was gone. Managing, great tyre wear - a league of his own."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted it wasn't the way he wanted to win and that Lando Norris deserved the Spanish GP victory

Why did Norris not stay out and pit later?

McLaren had the option to not pit Norris straight away so he could potentially build a gap to his rivals, particularly as Charles Leclerc stayed out and was holding up Antonelli.

However, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella says Norris' medium tyres were too worn and he would not have enough pace to pull away.

"We considered staying out but you have to accept the fact that now you're on relatively used medium tyres and the people behind you will be on new hards, so you're never going to open a gap on people on new hards," said Stella.

"Therefore, we kind of needed to accept that was what we should have done. And the fact that it was incredibly unfortunate. Sometimes we talk about being unlucky. I think at times that being unlucky is used for too many applications, but in this case, it's almost a mathematical definition of being unlucky."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris lost the race lead after an unlucky sequence of events which saw a missed a pitstop opportunity under a VSC, followed by a very slow stop by McLaren

Change the rules or part of racing?

Virtual Safety Cars were introduced to Formula 1 in 2015 following Jules Bianchi's tragic accident at the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix.

An indirect consequence of them is drivers drive to a delta which sees them go 30 to 40 per cent slower compared to green flag conditions.

The same rules initially apply when there's a full Safety Car, before the field gets bunched up, but it means a sporting advantage can be gained by pitting.

"It is racing and it's happened, so I can't really complain about it. I can be upset about it, but I can't really complain about it," said Norris.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted he felt bad for Lando Norris on team radio as he wins the first F1 race at the Madring

"I think there are things, because we have spoken about it in the past several times, about how it can be at least covered for one lap or everyone has the opportunity to do the pit stops, or you just block the pit entry and no one can box apart from if you have a puncture or something.

"So, I think there are a few things you could do to make it more simple and more fair for everyone, but that's a bigger discussion. This is not something I can just ask for."

Norris' maiden win at the 2024 Miami Grand Prix came with the help of a Safety Car which enabled him to have a cheaper pit stop against Max Verstappen.

But he pointed out that a rule change would require all drivers to come together to agree on new regulations.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Lando Norris slams the ending of the Virtual Safety Car, which led to him losing the Spanish Grand Prix

"I think we would all want, but there's a lot more to it. Depending on if it's raining and there's a VSC and you're on slicks, does it mean you can box or not? So it's a complicated subject," he said.

"But I think as a collection of drivers, if we all talk about it, I think everyone wants the same thing, and that's just fairness for everyone. Of course I'm complaining about it today, [but] I could benefit from it next week, next time out, and I could win because of it.

"I have to take it on the chin, but I just hope it doesn't happen to anyone again because it's just not how you should lose a race."

Sports.title: ‘An error of judgement’: Pro Ref admits mistake in awarding Haaland’s derby winner
Sports.content:
Pro Ref admitted Erling Haaland’s winner in Sunday’s Manchester derby should not have been awarded, after the video assistant referee ruled Enzo Fernández was not interfering with play in the buildup. The elite officiating body will review the decision and has contacted Manchester United.

Haaland’s 60th minute strike for Manchester City at Old Trafford was initially ruled offside before the VAR’s intervention. It came after Josko Gvardiol’s cross hit Patrick Dorgu’s boot, passed Fernández and the United defender Lisandro Martínez, and was finished by the City No 9. VAR decided Fernández was not interfering despite Martínez marking the midfielder.

A Pro Ref statement said: “Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday’s Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland’s awarded goal.

“The on-field decision was offside against Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position.

“In the same attack, it was established that Fernández did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review.

“Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.”

After the match but before the Pro Ref statement, an unhappy Michael Carrick expressed concern over Haaland’s winner.

“At the time I hadn’t totally seen it. But the explanation I got was he wasn’t interfering with play, so I just don’t get it,” the United manager said. “I can’t understand how they’re trying to help referees and putting so many layers behind them with so many people, screens, and so many whatever offices to try and come up with the right decisions.

“If that’s how the rules are interpreted, that you’re not interfering with play because you’ve thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Lisandro has to react from – it’s worrying if that’s really how the game’s seen by those who are officiating it.”

Carrick was asked if an apology from Pro Ref would be welcome. “Yeah, that’d be great, that. Yeah, I can’t wait for that one,” he said. “I don’t really know how you go and get another explanation on that one. I think we all understand what that rule means [regarding interfering with play], and it’s pretty obvious. It’s as obvious as it gets.”

Enzo Maresca, though, was adamant that Fernández was not interfering. “Yeah – and the fourth official said Erling is onside,” the City manager said.

The 199th Manchester derby’s other controversial decision was Phil Foden’s 23rd-minute red card. The forward kicked Bruno Fernandes in the stomach, but only after United’s captain had kicked him. Maresca backed Michael Oliver’s red card but suggested the referee should also have sent off Fernandes.

“Phil Foden red card is a red card, but I also think it is red card from Bruno,” City’s manager said. “Reviewing the action, it is a clear red card for Phil because it is a reaction but you can also see Bruno’s [action].”

City now have 12 points, second only to Arsenal on goal difference, while United have only four points and are 13th. “We will get there, I’m convinced of that,” Carrick said.

View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick looks on from the touchline during the Manchester derby. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

“We haven’t got as many points as we wanted and we should have. We’ve got to accept that and take that. It doesn’t change us moving forward and our hopes for the season and what we can achieve as a team. We’ve made really good strides over a period of time and we will continue to do that.”

Carrick was asked about the pre-game protest against the club’s move to eradicate ticket touts that some believe to be draconian. United said on Friday that 685 accounts had been subject to a ban and 464 supporters had received a reduced sanction or final warning.

Carrick said: “The details in terms of all what goes behind it, I’m not always in line to get to the bottom of it, but I definitely appreciate the supporters.

“If they do feel [unhappy] in certain ways then, of course, we want to try everything to make them happy. That’s part of performances on the pitch and off the pitch. That’s obvious. They’re a huge part of this football club. They’re everything for this football club.”

Inside the stadium The Red Army hung a banner over the tunnel that said, “The Way You Treat Us Is A Disgrace.” All usual banners were removed from the Stretford End.

Sports.title: Arteta embraces perfect storm to play the victim in game of his own making | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
A gentleman is never rude unintentionally, only by design. Nobody really knows who said this first. But it could easily be a line from the Elite Football Manager’s Guide to Press Conferences (Premier League edition). Because nothing happens by accident in these spaces.

Every word spoken in front of the board covered in adverts is metered and planned. A manager is never angry, or concerned, or even charming unintentionally. The game is the game, but so are all the other bits spilling out either side of it.

It was hard not to think about this while listening to Mikel Arteta talk about the penalty awarded to Sunderland at the Stadium of Light for a perceived act of grappling on Dan Ballard by Ezri Konsa. This is said with genuine professional respect. As everyone who has ever done a podcast knows – and this is, let’s be clear, everyone – there are lost Amazonian tribes discussing Girls season three in their own dark corner of Spotify – there are moments when you just have to flip the switch, up the energy and turn on full clip‑this‑bit‑up‑please‑Dave sincerity mode.

Arteta did this beautifully in the moment, appearing genuinely struck by what he was saying, radiating wounded integrity, like a disappointed junior headmaster appealing for the return of the school minibus keys.

Let’s be clear though. Arteta is not “very worried” about all this. He’s not “sad” or indeed, as he later emphasised for good measure, “really sad”. He’s not concerned solely with “protecting the game”, speaking here for all of us, just a fan of football.

Come off it. This is a manager we know to be obsessed with the most marginal of gains, to micro-plan the micro-details. As is all elite sport now. There has been talk of rowing coaches installing fibreglass toilet seats at their training hubs having calculated the average athlete spends 20 minutes in there and this is all key glute management time. Arteta loves this stuff. There’s no way Ben White isn’t sat fiddling with his phone at the training ground on a gold-standard Easy‑Cup Mega-Soft Evacu-Throne.

So it is with his public statements. This will have all been gamed and contingency‑planned in advance. And for hard, rational, tactical reasons, because this is how the game is played and run now. So what does it mean?

View image in fullscreen Ezri Konsa is penalised for a contentious foul on Dan Ballard in the box. Photograph: MI News/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

There are three things we know for sure. First, Arteta was right. This was a bad refereeing decision. Most obviously it was factually wrong. Ballard very skilfully pulled Konsa down on top of him, while simultaneously feigning shock that such a thing could happen.

It was doubly bad because the referee’s response was pre-planned, flagged by the early-season chat about refereeing in a more interventionist fashion. Go into any situation with a voice in your head, a vaguely worded mission to fulfil: this will skew your judgment.

The second thing is that referees are not biased. They’re just not very good. Two things have happened to them. First, the barrage of information to be absorbed in real time during a game is now utterly mind-boggling.

Most referees are not from a high-pressure data-processing background. These are not military pilots or traders on a currency floor. Less than a quarter have an academic degree. The task is beyond them. This is not a slur or an insult. It’s a simple description of what is happening, as supported by the evidence.

This is doubly annoying because referees have become fundamentally confused about their role. Referees are not ringmasters, or curators of the spectacle. They don’t get to decide what our sport should look like. Pro Ref is a private company with no locus standi to rule on the aesthetics of football. A referee should exist at the very edge of the spectacle. You’re not a local government planning officer with a mandate to decide which double-glazed French doors are or aren’t in character with the neighbourhood. Stop getting football not just wrong, but wrong.

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta has a word with the fourth official, Elliot Bell, at Sunderland. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

But Arteta was also ready for this. Arsenal’s coaches will have known this would happen at some point. That press conference response was already in the chamber. Arteta may even have practised his sad-not-angry face, his key lines.

And this would be the correct thing to do. None of this is breaking the rules, just as Arsenal are not a dirty team or a bunch of cheats. They play the game that is being presented to us, a sport that is being made to operate at the edge of its own ludicrously micro‑analysed rules on small issues of physical contact.

Arteta’s Arsenal have been masterful at finding advantages in this. Defenders are very good at playing with the ball at their feet now. Defenders are not selected for their ability to resist physical challenges. It is logical to exploit this, just as it is logical to seek to protect your ability to do so by speaking in public about how the rules are applied. This is why Arteta is good, and why he wins.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It is also true that this has created a strange environment. The tone of the wider Arsenal fanbase is another element here. There is no one type of football fan. All human life is here. But the fact remains, the loudest voices in the online Arsenal hive mind, even the atmosphere in the stadium is unique in its absolute conviction of victimhood, of conspiracy, of a galvanising sense of adversity.

There is no other ground where every single refereeing decision, even the who-knows 50-50s, is so violently and eloquently disputed. There are supporters who seem to spend most of the game up on their feet in a state of performative, weaponised indignation, whose entire interaction with the spectacle is an attitude of aggrieved injustice.

This makes sense, too. It speaks directly to the game we have created. Aggrieved middle-aged rule pedantry. This is the new cauldron of hate.

View image in fullscreen Set-piece grappling was a theme once more in Arsenal’s win at Sunderland. Photograph: Ian Hodgson/AP

Is it based in reality? Not perhaps on the outline numbers. Arsenal have been awarded more fouls than any other team this season. Only six teams last season had more fouls awarded against them, and the same the year before. They had the fewest yellow cards last season. They haven’t had a single red since they had six of them in 2024‑25.

Still, certain key incidents continue to grate and fester. There was the incorrectly denied penalty claim for Bruno Guimarães at Aston Villa. The balls-up with VAR lines against Brentford in 2023, which, if it really was deliberate conspiracy-cheating, was the worst, most public attempt at deliberate conspiracy-cheating ever conceived.

There is discontent at the way some rules seem to be applied more severely to Arsenal, the silly little stuff like delaying or fiddling about with restarts. But then again, if you make the game about that, if you plan to play on the margins, and successfully so, more stuff might happen in that place while you’re doing it.

Arteta has also played the role of arms-length rage conjurer expertly, has gone from rarely commenting on referees to heartfelt and carefully targeted critic. The Sunderland penalty award was a first opportunity to unload on the refereeing backlash to Arsenal’s tactics, to launch his pre-prepared defence; and to point out something demonstrably true. Referees have lost control of this, because the game has got beyond them.

In many ways this was a perfect storm for Arteta. Not just a decision that didn’t matter, because the penalty was saved. But a decision that was clearly incorrect too, a chance to get your lobbying in while very obviously in the right.

There will be more of this as the season plays out, as Arsenal work to preserve the advantages they have made for themselves in close quarters, tactical attack and defence. Factor in that masterful turn at a press conference j’accuse, and Saturday was a significant win in more ways than one.

Sports.title: Lewis Dunk’s showstopper helps five-star Brighton to rout 10-man Coventry
Sports.content:
The bare facts are bleak: Coventry City are only the second team in Premier League history to lose their first four games of the season ­without scoring a goal. “And yet …” will be the enduring message from Frank ­Lampard to his players.

And yet they have caused prob­lems for opposition teams. And yet they have already faced three of the top flight’s European contingent. And yet they are not altogether playing that badly – the Brighton goalkeeper Bart ­Verbruggen being named player of the match can attest to that. But Coventry des­perately need a point, or even a goal, to give their ­confidence a much-needed boost. It does not take long for a promoted club’s relegation fears to turn to reality.

Goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouyé, Lewis Dunk – especially – and Yasin Ayari were all moments of individual brilliance. But there was also a sense of Coventry self-destruction, with no complaints from Lampard over Taiwo Awoniyi’s red card for an elbow into Maxim De Cuyper’s face, nor the penalty conceded by Bobby Thomas for Pascal Gross to score the ­visitors’ third. There are also legitimate questions to be asked of Lampard’s decision to maintain an attacking approach even after the sending off.

“It’s a difficult scoreline and it’s not easy at home,” Lampard said. “The first half was pretty good, we created some chances, better chances and we had them under a lot of pressure. Then a mistake to make it 2-0 and the red card makes it very difficult.

“It feels very difficult to take the result, but a lot of circumstances that you can reflect on and say: ‘If, and if, and if.’ We need to be honest about that – we need to take chances in this league. It’s not a nice feeling.”

The scoreline certainly lent weight to Fabian Hürzeler’s insistence that Brighton have no attacking concerns despite Danny Welbeck’s summer departure. Brighton have scored more goals and created more big chances than any other club in the Premier League this season – indeed, they have never started a top‑flight campaign with more goals.

“It’s not about having one good goalscorer,” Hürzeler said. “It’s about the flexibility of having many goalscorers and a lot of players who have this desire to score. We were very efficient today and quite ruthless at the right moments in front of goal.”

That was certainly true, beginning with a moment of mastery from ­Kostoulas to break the deadlock, when the Greek teenager showed great poise to control an aerial ball with his foot, nod it between two defenders and then fire into the bottom corner.

That Brighton were not already behind by then was thanks to ­Verbruggen, who produced two excellent saves to deny Jack Rudoni, when palming a volley and a header to safety.

Lampard publicly urged his ­players to “have belief” during the half‑time interval, but then followed two ­minutes that instantly extinguished Coventry’s hopes.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard endures another glum day in the Premier League with Coventry. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

First came Brighton’s second goal, when Yalcouyé was played in behind the Coventry defence, and the Ivorian’s pace kept all at bay before calmly slotting past Carl Rushworth.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Moments later, the hosts were reduced to 10 men. At first glance, contact appeared accidental between Awoniyi and De Cuyper. But, to the refe­ree Tony Harrington’s credit, he spotted the Nigerian had led with his elbow, prompting a straight red card. To compound matters, the stadium announcer chose that period to tell fans that train cancellations meant there would be no departures from the stadium for 90 minutes after the final whistle.

Thomas’s challenge to bring down Kostoulas inside his own box was as clear a penalty as will be awarded all season and Gross duly stuck the spotkick into the bottom corner.

By the time Dunk sealed the rout with the finest strike of his career – smashed into the top corner from 35 yards – the mass exodus had already begun. It was an outrageous hit, with Dunk saying: “I shocked myself, but it was lovely.”

That was followed in injury time by another excellent finish, this time from Ayari, curled from range into the ­bottom corner.

The only other team to lose their first four Premier League games without scoring were Crystal Palace in 2017‑18. Palace finished 11th that season, but need to pull the emergency Roy Hodgson cord. ­Coventry will hope he is not required here.

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Arsenal rue misses in Palace draw, Manchester City crush Villa
Sports.content:
Arsenal were left to rue 30 missed chances after dropping points in a 0-0 draw against Crystal Palace at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners hit the target nine times and had almost 80% possession but could not convert their superiority into goals. Promoted Palace put on a resilient performance, with the goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin batting away attempts from Alessia Russo, Chloe Kelly and Mariona Caldentey to earn another clean sheet.

The reigning champions, Manchester City, continued their winning start to the campaign with a dominant 4-1 victory against Aston Villa. Jade Rose broke the deadlock for City in the early stages, tapping home after Akane Okuma failed to claim a corner. Assisted by Khadija Shaw, Mary Fowler doubled the advantage with a low-driven strike into the bottom-right of the net.

Amalie Vangsgaard gave Andrée Jeglertz and his players a fright after converting Chasity Grant’s pass in the 42nd minute, but Shaw returned to the scoresheet after half-time to restore the two-goal cushion. City wrapped up the victory in added time when Lauren Hemp’s strike was deflected in by Mathilde Harviken.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw scores Manchester City’s third goal in their 4-1 win at Villa Park. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters

Brighton came from two goals down to snatch a last-minute equaliser at Birmingham City. The promoted hosts took an early lead through Oceane Hurtre, who capitalised on a lapse in concentration from Caitlin Hayes before running into the box and slotting past Chiamaka Nnadozie.

Lily Crosthwaite made it two in the second half with a low driven shot across the goalkeeper, but Brighton gathered momentum when Olivia García came off the bench to close the gap in the 77th minute. As Birmingham attempted to hold on for the win, Kiko Seike raced into the box with just a few seconds remaining and made the most of a small gap between Sophie Baggaley and the near post to score.

At Goodison Park, Charlton fell to a 1-0 defeat by Everton following an own goal and two red cards. After a goalless first half, things quickly went downhill for the promoted side when Ashleigh Neville saw red for a high boot which caught Ruby Mace. With 13 minutes of normal time to play, the visitors found themselves behind when Holly McNamara’s cross deflected off the leg of Leighanne Robe and into the net. In the latter stages, Charlton went down to nine players after the substitute Hawa Cissoko received two yellow cards in quick succession.
