Liverpool came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw against Tottenham thanks to a 60th-minute header from Aurelie Csillag. Spurs took the lead just before half-time when Signe Gaupset’s effort was deflected in off the foot of Liverpool’s Sam Kerr. The hosts levelled things up at the hour-mark after Csillag got in front of Lize Kop to head home Fuka Nagano’s cross.

Sports.title: Lauren James revels in free role as Chelsea show ‘respect’ by scoring five past Manchester United
Sports.content:
A swaggering Chelsea cast off any suggestion that they had lost the ability to kill off games, putting five goals past a worryingly lacklustre and lackadaisical Manchester United.

Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea manager, said: “When you have the opportunity to really hurt a team, the best way to respect them is to score as many goals as you can, to create as many opportunities as you can.

“Of course, it’s never easy to see the other team or the other manager concede five goals because if I was the other team, I would be really sad. For me, showing respect to the opponent is having that desire and mentality to score as many goals as possible. That’s the difference between the great teams and the good teams.”

United’s players and fans may have preferred disrespect if that is the case. Instead, it was another bruising result for the new manager, Eva Olid, and her side after an underwhelming performance in their 2-1 defeat against London City Lionesses in the opening game of the season.

Olid needed a result to give her some breathing room and her team some confidence, having had just three weeks to get used to one another before the start of the season, and this early into a project there has to be some grace.

For their opponents this game had been talked about as something of a must‑win after the Blues were held to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villa on the opening weekend despite dominating that match.

View image in fullscreen Keira Walsh scores Chelsea’s side's second goal from the edge of the box. Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images

To some extent the concern over Chelsea’s profligacy did not need to be too deep. They were at their creative best against Villa and were without the injured centre-forwards Melvine Malard and Mayra Ramírez while Aggie Beever-Jones, who led the line against the Midlands side, had not scored in the Women’s Super League since September 2025. The off-target Beever-Jones was relegated to the bench for the trip to United. Instead, Lauren James and Sjoeke Nüsken worked away interchangeably up front.

The visitors were similarly fluid in other areas too, and that flexibility was super effective. Chelsea were unpredictable and James’s free‑to‑roam role put their star talent at the centre of everything.

Lucy Bronze’s marauding forward yielded the opener when she sent a looping ball over the top and Dominique Janssen should have been first to it, but the United defender misread the fall of the ball and a stalking Wieke Kaptein nipped it away from her. The Dutch midfielder squared to Nüsken who fired in from close range.

The second goal, which eluded them against Villa, arrived just over 10 minutes later. A diving header from the new recruit Andrea Medina cleared a cross whipped in from the left but the hard-working Bronze was there to meet it, clipping it into the path of Keira Walsh, who took a step and powered in from the edge of the box.

The hosts’ heads dropped, which left their manager unhappy. “In football we know anything can happen,” Olid said. “You can be losing 2-0 and can end up winning. I don’t like the heads down. Heads up and we have to continue. Everything is about confidence.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A very brief brighter spell for United after the break was snuffed out by the visiting team and James finally got on the scoresheet after the hour, latching on to Walsh’s defence‑splitting pass and shrugging off Janssen before sending a low drive into the net.

Chelsea’s fourth goal rubbed salt in for a very wounded United side. Janssen, under no pressure, failed to respond to an ambitious burst from Kaptein and the Chelsea midfielder pickpocketed the centre-back and slipped the ball wide to the onrushing Ellie Carpenter, whose first effort was kept out by Phallon Tullis‑Joyce but her follow-up found the net.

Bronze then added to United’s misery during the final minute of added time, hammering the ball in after Walsh knocked a corner back into the melee in the six-yard box.

It became a training exercise for Chelsea and the hosts failed in their attempts to limit the damage. Things look as if they will get worse for Olid’s side before they get better, with a trip to the Emirates Stadium to play Arsenal coming up next weekend, but Olid said she will not divert from the style of football she wants the team to commit to playing.

“If you start changing, then you are never going to build what you want to build,” she said. “It’s a process. I know it’s so hard, the process, because this beginning is hard. Nobody wants to lose games, but we have to be faithful to what we want to do, because I think that long term will give us the wins.”

Sports.title: European football: Lamine Yamal keeps Barcelona perfect, Leipzig rout Hamburg
Sports.content:
Barcelona continued their perfect start to the ⁠season with a hard-fought 4-2 La Liga victory over Levante in Valencia ⁠on Sunday.

Levante ⁠found ​themselves two goals down within 19 minutes after swift play from ⁠Barcelona led to goals for Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal. The home side ⁠then rallied, finishing the half with six ​shots to Barcelona’s ‌three.

Just 42 ‌seconds into the second half, Barcelona were awarded ‌a penalty, won and converted by Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old now has three doubles in his past three La Liga matches.

An errant pass from Espart allowed Levante forward Iván Romero ‌to round goalkeeper Joan García and pass the ball into the net ​with 12 minutes to go. With two minutes remaining, Roger Brugue burst through multiple Barcelona challenges to score a second for Levante.

The ⁠home side’s hopes of a draw were definitively ​ended ​by a mazy run ​and finish from Karim Adeyemi ​in the ‌93rd minute.

Barcelona ​are alone ​at the top of the table with five wins from five, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

Atlético Madrid scored three late goals ​to beat Real Sociedad 3-0, as new ​signings Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David scored their ​first goals since joining the club.

Both sides struggled to create clear chances until Grimaldo netted an 84th-minute penalty, ​before David doubled their lead ‌after finding space on ​the break six minutes later.

Giuliano ​Simeone added a third in the 95th minute to complete the scoring for Atlético, who were without Julián Alvarez and Pablo Barrios due to muscle injuries as they returned to winning ways after two consecutive losses.

Málaga rescued a 1-1 draw against Celta Vigo, who had dominated the game at Balaidos, while Deportivo A Coruña also drew 1-1 with Getafe after going behind in the second half.

Harry Kane scored his first goal of the season to help Bayern Munich edge to a 2-1 win at promoted Elversberg in the Bundesliga on Sunday. Handed the captain’s armband with skipper Manuel Neuer rested, Kane scored with 18 minutes remaining to break a 1-1 deadlock and put the defending champions on track for victory.

Bayern had taken the lead through teenage Germany winger Lennart Karl but Elversberg levelled things up just after the hour mark thanks to a stunning curling effort from Maurice Krattenmacher.

Kane scored 36 league goals last campaign but after drawing a blank in his first two matches he told Dazn: “That’s football – sometimes you have to wait more than you’d have expected.

“It was nice to get the goal and the three points. It’s a tough place so we’re happy with the win… We probably haven’t reached our top level yet, but it’s still early days.”

RB Leipzig bounced back from their Champions League defeat at Como by thumping strugglers Hamburg 5-0 at home.

Norway winger Antonio Nusa was the best of the bunch for the hosts, scoring one goal and setting up two more, including one for Christopher Nkunku, the French winger’s first since returning to Leipzig in August.

Tidiam Gomis, Willi Orban and Romulo also got on the scoresheet for Leipzig, who climbed to fourth with the victory.

“It’s easy to look into the past too much. You lost two games. It’s difficult, but you have to look forward,” Nusa said.

“Today we had to perform and we did, so I think we had a good balance of not thinking too much of the past, but trying to attack today and I think we did it.”

Hamburg’s third big defeat in their third league match this campaign leaves the six-time German champions in bottom spot in the table.

In Italy Juventus suffered a 3-2 defeat after a frantic finish at Sassuolo on Sunday, while Napoli ended a three-match losing run with a ⁠1-0 home win over ⁠Bologna as both ​sides continued their inconsistent starts to the Serie A season.

After a largely uneventful first hour, Sassuolo broke the deadlock in the 65th minute when Nemanja Matic slipped a precise ⁠pass into the area for Sebastiano Esposito, who finished with a slick one-touch stroke. Juventus levelled in the 82nd ​minute after Sassuolo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric misjudged a cross, ‌allowing Edon Zhegrova to tap ‌into an empty net.

The hosts thought they had sealed victory in the 89th minute when Darryl Bakola teed ‌up Kieron Bowie, who curled a first-time effort into the corner. Zhegrova appeared to have rescued a point for Juventus when he fired home from the edge of the area in stoppage time to complete his brace, but Sassuolo had the final say.

Four minutes into stoppage time, Vasilije Adzic controlled a deep cross and curled in a superb finish into the far corner to seal victory for Sassuolo with virtually the ‌last kick of the game.

Napoli ended their recent slump as Stanislav Lobotka turned in a second-half winner to secure all three points at the Stadio Diego Armando ​Maradona.

The home side dominated possession early on, but Bologna thought they had taken the lead in the seventh minute when Arthur Theate headed home. The effort was ruled out for offside following a VAR ⁠review.

Lobotka eventually broke the deadlock in the 66th minute, scoring the game’s only goal ​to hand Napoli all three points.

In Ligue 1 Paris Saint-Germain won their first match of the season ⁠and Ferran ⁠Torres kept up ​his goalscoring form with the only goal of the game in a 1-0 win at Brest on Sunday.

Torres took five minutes to put PSG ahead, picking up ⁠a loose ball in midfield, passing to João Neves, then Ousmane Dembélé, whose back heel into Torres’ path gave the Spaniard time to bend a low shot into the corner.

Torres has now netted ⁠six goals in five outings since moving to the European champions after scoring the winner for Spain in July’s World Cup ​final against Argentina in New York.

Earlier, Lens fought back from two goals down ‌to draw 2-2 at promoted Le Mans while Lille went top of the table after an easy 2-0 triumph over Troyes.

The victory put Lille top with 10 points from four matches, ahead of ​Monaco and Rennes on goal difference.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans in Saudi Pro League after Diogo Jota chants
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo said that fans who appeared to ⁠make chants referencing his former teammate Diogo Jota at Rúben Neves during a Saudi ⁠Pro League ⁠match ​should be banned for life from football stadiums.

The chants occurred on Saturday during ⁠a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves’s side, Al-Hilal, in Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.

Jota died last year in a car crash in Zamora, ​north-western Spain, along with ‌his brother André ‌Silva. A close friend of Jota, Neves was a ‌pallbearer at his funeral.

Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting “Jota”. The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who pointed to his eye and ‌then up to the sky in response. Passing through the mixed zone after the game, ​Neves said: “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”

In response to an Instagram post showing the footage, Ronaldo commented from his personal account. “The league must take ⁠action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” he wrote. “This ​is no longer football, ​and there have to be limits. People ​who behave ‌like this should ​never ​be allowed to enter a stadium again.“

The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted.

Reuters has contacted Al-Taawoun and Al-Hilal for comment.

Sports.title: Rangers lay down Old Firm marker to send Celtic packing from Scottish League Cup
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes has endured a much‑scrutinised start to life at Ibrox but the Rangers manager got the old ground bouncing here as his side dominated Celtic in front of an all-blue crowd to decide the first Old Firm encounter of the season.

Against a backdrop of bouncing techno from the tannoy, Rangers fans celebrated three memorable goals in a thumping League Cup win. A brace for the captain, Dan Neil, bookended Kevin Kelsy’s second‑half finish to put Martin O’Neill’s side down with relative ease. It also showcased a nascent identity for McInnes’s side, one defined by unbending physical commitment and lots and lots of sprinting. The quality of the football may have been patchy, but the commitment was enough to get the 51,212 home fans at the top of their voices.

With away fans banned from Old Firm fixtures this season after the pitch invasion that followed a Scottish Cup tie in March, the atmosphere was always likely to be partisan, if perhaps less heated than is customary. Before the match there was a brisk trade on both Graeme Souness flags and boiled sweets. Inside the ground the Union Bears ultras unveiled a tifo showcasing the apparently resonant moment when Rangers’ Ian Ferguson grabbed Celtic’s Mike Galloway by the lapels during a clash in 1993. A deep cut of a banner, it did a good job of setting the tone for what was to follow.

McInnes said: “I’m delighted. The performance we gave today was the one required to overcome a team like Celtic. I thought the game demanded the players’ full attention and I’m delighted they’ve managed to deliver that. We’ve seen the strength of the club today and it does the players no harm to understand what this match means to so many people.”

Rangers went about the match with an intensity that Celtic struggled to equal from the off, some of their players looking distinctly overawed by the occasion. The former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was among them, flapping at two early openings, but he could do nothing about the opening goal when it arrived in the 22nd minute. After a Celtic counter broke down Rangers immediately turned play around with a long ball to the Celtic area where Cameron Carter‑Vickers failed to properly clear. Kelsy picked up the loose ball, slipped it to Neil and the captain, signed on a free transfer from Sunderland in the summer, placed an excellent shot just inside Johnstone’s left‑hand post.

After seizing the advantage, Rangers went on to dominate the second half and a second goal appeared inevitable. It duly arrived when a free-kick from the impressive James Penrice was flicked on by Ryan Naderi to the back post where Kelsy clipped his effort around the keeper and inside the left-hand post.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Kelsy lashes in Rangers’ second goal around the hour. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Neil then took matters into his own hands with a quarter of an hour remaining as he controlled a loose ball on the edge of the Celtic area and wrapped a shot into the top corner to unleash delirium in the Copland Stand. “I haven’t scored many goals in my career, so to come away with a brace is immense,” Neil said.

It was perhaps just as well for O’Neill that his supporters had been denied access to this match. Celtic began with a calmness that suggested confidence. Ultimately it was more likely to have reflected timidity. The Bhoys were unable to get a foot on the ball at all in the second half, and the big-money signing Kasper Høgh looked lost at the tip of the Celtic attack before he was substituted on 65 minutes.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We were well beaten in the end, on the day we were second best,” O’Neill said. “There has to be a realisation how big this game is, it’s still one of the great fixtures in European football if not the world. We’ve got to know that. We have to learn from it. Hopefully it’s a wake‑up call.”

Rangers will play Aberdeen in the semi-finals, but McInnes was still being asked about Rangers’ stuttering start to the season after this match, generating the timeless response: “Why are you pissing on my chips?”

After this result the Rangers manager can at least look forward with optimism and he could be set to unleash the spirit of Ian Ferguson again as early as next weekend when a second Old Firm derby awaits, this time at Celtic Park.

Sports.title: Allowing Erling Haaland's match-winning Manchester derby goal was a MISTAKE, admits referees' body, after Michael Carrick's side fumed over baffling decision
Sports.content:
Referees’ bosses last night admitted it was a mistake not to rule out Erling Haaland’s controversial winning goal in the Old Trafford derby. Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick was furious after Haaland’s strike gave City’s 10 men a 1-0 win, and defender Lisandro Martinez branded the decision an ‘injustice’. VAR official Matt Donohue incorrectly allowed the goal to stand even though Enzo Fernandez was offside when he challenged Martinez for the ball in front of goal, on the basis that City’s new £125million signing did not touch it. However, the rules state that a player in an offside position will be penalised if they impact an opponent by attempting to play the ball. A statement from Pro Ref confirmed: 'Following the incident in the 60th minute of Sunday's Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Manchester City at Old Trafford, we can provide clarification regarding Erling Haaland's awarded goal. 'The on-field decision was offside against Erling Haaland – that was checked by VAR and he was found to be in an onside position. Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) September 13, 2026 Pro Ref have apologised to Manchester United after Erling Haaland's controversial goal in the Manchester derby was allowed to stand Haaland's goal was given after a VAR review, with it having originally been ruled offside However, Enzo Fernandez was in an offside position and attempted to go for the ball 'In the same attack, it was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective, however, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review. 'Contact has been made with Manchester United this evening to acknowledge what we deem is an error of judgement. A review of the incident will take place.' While Haaland celebrated a record ninth Premier League goal in the Manchester derby, Martinez was fuming. 'It's the best league in the world, you have the best teams in the world, the best players in the world, and now we have to go home with this injustice,' he said. 'I think it was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He (Fernandez) was there, in front of me, and I went to him. So that's why Haaland was free at the back. 'It's so hard because you lose a derby and you lose three points at home. Every season they're coming to our club and explaining the rules for an hour-and-a-half. They look so confident, and then after that five or six people are making these kind of mistakes. It's unacceptable.' United head coach Michael Carrick was just as upset as Martinez, saying: 'I really don't get it. 'I can't understand how they're trying to help referees by putting so many layers behind them – with so many people, so many bodies, so many screens – and you're not interfering with play because you've thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and nearly touched it. 'It's worrying if that's really how the game's seen by those who are officiating it.' When it was mentioned to Carrick that Pro Ref have issued apologies in the past, he replied sarcastically: 'That would be great, I can't wait for that one! It's best left, I think. I don't really know how you go and get another explanation on that one.' A furious Lisandro Martinez claimed that United were the victims of an 'injustice' At the time of the incident, Gary Neville had been left confused on Sky Sports' commentary and criticised the decision, insisting the officials had got things wrong. He said: 'I will need the offside explained to me. The officials will be nervous about this goal. 'When they look back on this, they will recognise they got this wrong. The question is does Fernandez, who is offside, stop Martinez getting the ball? He does.' When reminded that the rules state a player can still be offside even if they don't touch the ball, Neville replied: 'They're the words that I think – emphatically – mean we will see an apology from Pro Ref. 'There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off. 'It's a really strange one. They'll recognise they got that wrong.' Before Pro Ref's apology, the Premier League Match Centre had attempted to explain the reasoning for the goal being awarded. On their X account, they wrote: 'VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. 'The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball.' Meanwhile, Foden was shown a straight red card by referee Michael Oliver when he retaliated to Fernandes kicking him in the back while he was on the ground by lashing out at the United captain. City boss Enzo Maresca said: 'Phil Foden's red card is red card, but I also think it's a red card for Bruno. To win a game with 10 players is special, but it is even more special when it is Manchester derby.'

Sports.title: From the moment stupid Phil Foden was sent off, there was only one team playing smart, cute football... and it wasn't Man United, who fell straight into City's trap, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Manchester City have inflicted a few embarrassments on their neighbours in modern times and now they have done it again. Another big day out at Old Trafford. Another victory. Another song to sing.

The cast may be different but the story remains the same. City blue looking at United red in the rear-view mirror.

This was a victory that had controversy written right through it.

Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes in only the 23rd minute. Foden was provoked by a sly Fernandes kick that itself warranted some kind of punishment that never came. But the City player was stupid and reckless. He had to go.

As for the winning goal – poked in at the far post midway through the second half by Erling Haaland – it is hard to work out why it was allowed to stand. Initially ruled out by a linesman, the decision was bafflingly, and as it turns out incorrectly, overturned by VAR.

Enzo Fernandes – chief City pest all day – didn’t make contact with the ball as it passed in front of him on the six-yard line. But he clearly tried to and – given that was a yard offside – that should have been enough to see the initial call confirmed.

Man City beat Man United 1-0 at Old Trafford despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half

Erling Haaland scored the winner despite the fact his goal caused significant controversy

He was originally called offside before VAR intervened, but Enzo Fernandez (No 17) was in an offside position and appeared to interfere with play

Why wasn’t it? Well let’s just say it seems we have now reached the arguably inevitable juncture when referees, VAR officials and their paymasters no longer understand their own rules. Join the club, lads.

So United have reason to feel aggrieved. But the fact remains that from the moment Foden walked, there was only one team playing smart, cute football and it wasn’t Michael Carrick’s.

United hit the post twice from distance – Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – while Gianluigi Donnarumma made perhaps the save of the season to deny Bryan Mbeumo in the fourth minute of five added. No wonder his team-mates ran to the big Italian at the end. Donnarumma has had a difficult time of late but this was a reminder of his star quality.

But where City were clever and intelligent and in control as they drew the sting and the energy out of United, their opponents were suckered in to playing a game that didn’t suit them.

In the City midfield, Fernandez was a defining influence and is destined to become a hero in that part of town. Meanwhile, Elliot Anderson schooled United’s Kobbie Mainoo in a way that shows just why he plays for England and his opponent doesn’t.

England manager Thomas Tuchel was here to see this ahead of naming a squad on Friday but you didn’t have to have a trained eye to see the trail of quality Anderson left across this football pitch. United tried to sign him, too. Ouch.

At the end City’s joy was unconfined. New manager Enzo Maresca was off down the touchline like a bunny. It wasn’t quite full Jose Mourinho but it had all the same vibes. With Arsenal setting a furious pace at the top of the league, City cannot afford to lose many. As such, this was a big result for reasons above and beyond those that involve the mood that the people of Manchester take in to work with them the next morning.

From the start, it had felt like a big afternoon for both clubs. But then when isn’t it when the derby rolls around? For all the fakery and false narratives imposed upon us by the Premier League’s corporate machine these days, this is a rivalry that remains very real.

City are only a few games into Maresca’s evolution while United remain a curious mix of optimism and self-harm. The four goals Carrick’s team had scored in the Champions League last Thursday will have helped their self-esteem. But this was different. It was a real opponent.

Maresca rolled his dice in terms of his attacking line up and had clearly instructed his players to get on the front foot. It was an approach that had served them well here before but was one that was tempered once Foden made that long diagonal walk across the Old Trafford turf and off down its famous corner tunnel.

It was a shame to see him go. Not only because Foden’s gradual re-emergence had slowly gathered pace this autumn but also because it changed the feel of the game. The opening quarter of the game had felt like a street fight. Not pretty but intense and adrenaline-charged. The sending off took some of the juice out of that as City dropped in to a shape and invited United to unlock them.

That wasn’t always going to suit the home team, as strange as it sounds. They remain a side most dangerous on the counter attack and had shown signs of that early on here, particularly when Rashford was invited to stretch City down United’s left flank.

With a man over and the scale of City’s ambition changing, United were asked to play in a way that does not altogether suit them.

Phil Foden was sent off after he kicked out at Bruno Fernandes having been fouled by him

This was a huge victory for Enzo Maresca as he made it four wins from four in the league so far

But this was a difficult day for Michael Carrick, whose side did nowhere near enough after Foden's dismissal

Earlier, it had been fractious. Twice in the opening two minutes, United players came crashing in to their opponents. First Diogo Dalot brought down Anderson and then Harry Maguire went through the dangerous Rayan Cherki.

It was not a one-way street for City, though. Over time and before the red card, United took a foothold. Rashford was always the main outlet but Fernandes was creative too. One chipped through pass had United roars in throats only for the recipient found to be Dalot, who could not control.

Haaland was quiet. He often is. Indeed for the first fifteen minutes he didn’t touch the ball. But then a Fernandes mistake invited him to charge through the middle and his pass towards Cherki on the right would have opened up had Lisandro Martinez not made an important interception.

Even before Foden departed, City struggled to control the rhythms and tempo of the game the way they often did here in the Pep Guardiola years. That said much for the way United had lifted their levels after last weekend’s disappointing draw at Everton. They looked at times like a team ready to take a big step forward. Sadly for them, that feel wasn’t to last.

Either side of the half-time break, Carrick’s team struck a post from distance. First Rashford did so from a 25-yard free-kick and then, in the 50th minute, Mainoo did likewise after running on to the ball in a central position just outside the penalty area at the Stretford End.

Rashford then drilled an effort in to the side netting with his left foot before Matheus Cunha drove over from the other side. As the hour mark approached, United were beginning to run hot. Maresca had replaced Cherki with Iliman Ndiaye at half-time but that had done nothing for his team at this juncture.

It felt as if a goal would come and soon it did. Incredibly, it was at the other end. Haaland had done nothing all day but his finish to Josko Gvardiol’s far post cross was superb. Haaland looked offside but wasn’t. Fernandez – diving at the ball as it came across - looked offside and was. Even so, City had an unlikely and rather confusing lead that would have been doubled had United goalkeeper Senne Lammens not touched Fernandez's low shot on to the inside of the post with his fingertips.

For United embarrassment beckoned and the tale of the game was to be found in the statistics. Despite their domination of ball and territory and despite two strikes against woodwork, it took them 50 minutes following Foden’s dismissal to register a shot on target. As we entered the last 15 minutes, they had to find something.

Instead, Haaland almost poked in a low Fernandes free-kick at the far post as the United back four wobbled again.

City, frankly, were proving themselves to be cleverer than their opponents. Now that United had to chase it, City drew fouls and wasted time. As they did so, United’s frustration grew.

Kobbie Mainoo struggled against counterpart Elliot Anderson, who was exceptional for City

Fernandez (No 17) was also a defining influence and managed to wind up United's players

Fernandez seemed to be at the heart of most of it but United should have risen above it and didn’t. They fell right into the City trap.

Bryan Mbeumo and Maguire both drifted headers wide as time wore on. There was no kitchen sink thrown though. There was no onslaught. It all felt a bit forlorn and hopeful.

Mbeumo’s chance at the death came on the back of an isolated moment of football intelligence.

Against any modern City side – old or new – you have to find something a bit better than that.

Sports.title: Moment Noel Gallagher's nepo baby son Sonny, 15, puts his middle fingers up at fans after Erling Haaland scores goal during Man City vs Man United match
Sports.content:
Moment Noel Gallagher's nepo baby son Sonny, 15, puts his middle fingers up at fans after Erling Haaland scores goal during Man City vs Man United match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Noel Gallagher's 15-year-old son was spotted giving the middle finger to Man United fans after Man City's Erling Haaland scored the controversial deciding goal at Old Trafford.

Sonny Gallagher celebrated alongside his brother Donovan, 18, and their Oasis rockstar father Noel, 59, in the stands 62 minutes into the game, with City a man down after Phil Foden's red card.

The teenager flipped off rival fans in the stands and jeered as star striker Haaland netted in the second-half what later proved to be the winner.

His gesture will have rubbed salt in the wounds as it came after a lengthy VAR check that the home supporters thought would rule out the strike for offside. But the goal was incorrectly awarded and gave City a lead they held on to.

Sonny's father, meanwhile, punched the air in jubilation and chanted, clapping as his youngest son gave both middle fingers to their opponents.

The Gallaghers are known for being die-hard Manchester City fans, and have been supporters long before the club became the dominant Premier League force it is today.

Oasis have been the musical backdrop of the successes that City has amassed since Sheikh Mansour bought the club in 2008.

Gallagher and his brother, Liam, have become the team's most recognisable supporters.

Sonny Gallagher (pictured in a blue jacket, second from left) gave the middle finger to Man United fans after his team scored a goal

He was watching the game alongside his brother Donovan (pictured second from left, in a grey jacket) and rockstar father Noel (third from left)

The moment Erling Haaland scored a goal against Man United, taking his team to a 1-0 victory

Noel is even close friends with the club's former manager, Pep Guardiola, who transformed the club over his nearly decade in charge.

On Sunday, Noel's sons were recognisable in the crowd, with Sonny donning a navy and blue jacket in his father's Mod rocker style.

It is the brothers' second outing with their celebrity father this week, after making an appearance at the premiere of Oasis: Don't Look Back In Anger in London.

Sonny was the spitting image of his rocker dad after borrowing his vintage 2008 Stone Island jacket for the event - with a matching haircut to fit.

Noel had worn the jacket at a press conference in Wembley to announce a stadium tour nearly two decades ago.

He declared at the time the shows would be 'the gigs of next year, if not the decade' after announcing they would perform for three nights at the arena.

Liam and Noel Gallagher proved that all past feuds were behind them by appearing together, fresh from an eight-minute standing ovation at the Venice Film Festival last weekend.

Liam and Noel's nepo baby brood were out in force earlier this week to support their fathers' upcoming documentary (from left to right: Lennon, Donovan, Anais, Molly, Sonny and Gene Gallagher)

They posed with their broods in Leicester Square, with the two brothers' children being united with their cousins after their parents' 15-year public spat.

The brotherly appearance was a far cry from the days of backstage bust-ups, walk-outs and booze-fuelled arguments in the public eye.

Beaming and wrapping their arms around each other on Monday night were Liam’s son Lennon, 26, Noel’s son Donovan, 18, and his model daughter Anais, 26.

They were joined by Liam’s daughter, Molly, 28, Sonny and Liam’s other boy Gene, 25.

The new Disney+ documentary chronicles their split and reconciliation, while following the band on their reunion tour last year.

Noel tells the Disney+ documentary that he and Liam’s children didn’t even know each other before the reunion tour.

'Donovan and Sonny had never met Gene and Lennon. Lo and behold they’re best friends now,' he said. Liam joked: ‘They’re off their heads every night. F****** spangled.'

Sports.title: Alexander Zverev's infuriating habit leaves US Open fans struggling to watch final against Ben Shelton
Sports.content:
Alexander Zverev's infuriating habit leaves US Open fans struggling to watch final against Ben Shelton

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tennis fans are growing impatient with German tennis star Alexander Zverev's frustrating pre-serve habit.

Zverev, the reigning French Open champion, is on Arthur Ashe this Sunday in the US Open men's singles final with the aim of beating American Ben Shelton to take his second Grand Slam title.

Throughout his run to the final, fans have noted that Zverev has a penchant for bouncing the ball repeatedly before his serve.

While bouncing the ball is not uncommon, Zverev does it to a level beyond what is considered the norm.

In an interview, he was asked about the habit and the German didn't provide much of a detailed answer to satisfy the masses.

'I have no idea why. I'm not doing it on purpose,' Zverev told reporters. 'I just, I saw the stat, like I bounced it 12,000 times or something like that. That was quite funny.'

Alexander Zverev was asked about how much he bounces the ball on serve 🤣



↳ US Open. Every Match. Live & On Demand.#StanSportAU #USOpen pic.twitter.com/2uTHhuKgcK — Stan Sport (@StanSportAU) September 12, 2026

Tennis fans are growing tired of Alexander Zverev's pre-serve habits at the US Open

Fans have debated Zverev's habit of bouncing the ball pre-serve an excessive amount of times

Zverev is in his second Grand Slam final of the year, playing Ben Shelton for the US Open crown

Zverev added: 'I mean, no, I'm not like, I'm not counting in my head. I'm not getting a certain number or anything like that. I don't know why it increased so much.

'I think today it decreased again. Because I saw it before the semifinals. So I was like, okay, it's got to go less. But then, like, I forget about it every once in a while, and then it goes up to— I don't know what number it is.'

When asked if there's anything specific that happens to get him to stop bouncing the ball, Zverev replied: 'No clue. Honestly, like, really honestly, no idea.'

The German's habit had fans angry on social media: 'It's almost always 16 times come on Sasha, you know it,' read one comment.

Another said: 'It's obviously a tactic.'

At the time of publishing, Zverev leads Shelton after winning the first two sets 6-3, 7-6 (7-2).

Sports.title: Chelsea target Lamine Camara breaks silence on dramatic collapse of £47m deadline-day move to Xabi Alonso's side
Sports.content:
Monaco's Lamine Camara has insisted that he has 'turned the page' after his £47.2million move to Chelsea dramatically collapsed minutes after the window closed on deadline day.

Chelsea thought they had secured the 22-year-old Senegal midfielder with less than two hours of deadline day remaining, having agreed a £47.2m deal. However, in an eventful twist, the Blues were left stunned and furious when Monaco then went back on their word.

Chelsea sources told Daily Mail Sport at the time that the two clubs had reached a full, written, club-to-club agreement for Camara to join.

Yet when Monaco renegotiated their transfer of Folarin Balogun to Everton, Chelsea were told that the six-year deal with the option of a one-year extension for Camara was being withdrawn. Insiders at Stamford Bridge described it as a deeply unprofessional way for another club to conduct business.

Camara appeared to be keen to draw a line under the situation ahead of Monaco's match against Strasbourg on Saturday.

He said: 'There was a possibility I could leave. It didn't go through at the last minute and that's part of football.

'I've turned the page and am focusing on the season.'

Monaco's Lamine Camara (right) has insisted that he has 'turned the page' after a £47.2million move to Chelsea dramatically collapsed minutes after the window closed on deadline day

The Blues had sanctioned the joint-record British transfer of Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for £125m on deadline day, but did so without having their own replacement at the ready.

Chelsea spent their deadline day chasing Camara, seeing two bids worth £38.5m and £42.9m turned down earlier in the day before having a third accepted.

And Chelsea sources added they had the opportunity to stop Fernandez from joining City after they learned of the U-turn on Camara – but they had given their word to their Premier League counterparts and, unlike Monaco, they honoured it.

Monaco have won their first three Ligue 1 fixtures of the season and sit second to Rennes in the table, with a game in hand, heading into the weekend.

'I can help the team a lot,' the Senegal international Camara added.

'Football moves fast. Maybe other opportunities will come along. But for now, I'm staying focused on the season with Monaco.'

Sports.title: Phil Foden is SENT OFF in Manchester derby: City bail out star after he is shown a straight red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes - but Roy Keane claims the United captain should have gone instead
Sports.content:
Phil Foden is SENT OFF in Manchester derby: City bail out star after he is shown a straight red card for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes - but Roy Keane claims the United captain should have gone instead

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City midfielder Phil Foden was sent off in the Manchester derby in stunning fashion after kicking out at Bruno Fernandes.

Old Trafford came alive in the first half-hour when Foden tussled with Manchester United's captain, with referee Michael Oliver adjudging that the England midfielder had violently kicked out.

Replays suggested Fernandes had kicked Foden while on the floor, and Foden responded by extending his legs into the stomach of Fernandes, and was given his marching orders.

Former United defender Gary Neville, who was sent off in a derby in 2004, said on Sky Sports: 'Oh dear. Oh dear, Phil Foden. He's not having it, he's hanging around. Bruno Fernandes has a bit of a kick at him while he's on the ground and Foden reacts. He's kicked him in the stomach. He's not going to get away with that.

'You can see why he is annoyed. He thinks Bruno has had a kick at him. But he reacts badly. VAR described it as a kick with both feet into the stomach.'

He would later brand the act 'a petulant little reaction' to being kicked on the floor, and added: 'If you do that on the floor it is measured differently to someone kicking on the floor. I think it is a yellow card for Fernandes.'

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL — Sky Sports Premier League (@SkySportsPL) September 13, 2026

Phil Foden (right) was sent off in the Manchester derby for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes (left)

Foden was given a straight red card as he protested his innocence to referee Michael Oliver

The ruling from VAR was that there was a 'secondary movement' from Foden and it was a 'clear red card'. It's unclear if there was any check on Fernandes' actions.

Foden is from Stockport in Greater Manchester but let his emotions get the better of him on this occasion.

England team-mate Marcus Rashford was among those calling for a red card, while Foden was consoled by the majority of his team-mates as he left the field.

Good friend and striker Erling Haaland, however, didn't see the need to give any love to the midfielder and angrily ordered him off the field. Haaland would later bail Foden out by scoring the winner in the game.

At half-time, attention turned to the actions of Fernandes, who had kicked Foden while he was on the floor, triggering a response.

Former United captain Roy Keane said on Sky Sports: 'He (Fernandes) goes and tackles him, gives him a little boot on the floor, he does react obviously. The strange thing is... I'm guessing it's classed as violent. To me, Bruno is the one who is violent.

'We see violence in a different way. I don't think that's a red card. Did the player give the referee a chance? Foden is daft, but so is Bruno. If Bruno got sent off we would be saying he is daft. Bruno has to do better there. Foden, I don't think it's a red card.'

Ex-City defender Micah Richards, meanwhile, added: 'Foden didn't react (in pain). If he reacted at the second kick... if Foden starts screaming, the decision is reversed.

An angry Erling Haaland ordered Foden from the field as other team-mates consoled him

Fernandes had seemed to kick out at Foden initially, triggering the response from the star

'As a referee, it looks worse than it is. I don't agree with the reaction from Foden, but Fernandes started it.'

It comes amid a tough run of form for the 26-year-old, who has not scored in 2026 and lost his England spot for the World Cup.

Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel was also in the crowd at Old Trafford to watch the game.

Foden was once Premier League player of the season, winning the award in the 2023-24 campaign, but he has struggled to produce performances since, and this is his latest setback.

Sports.title: More gloom and misery for Frank Lampard as Coventry's pointless - and goalless - start to the season leaves them rock bottom as Brighton run out 5-0 winners
Sports.content:
More gloom and misery for Frank Lampard as Coventry's pointless - and goalless - start to the season leaves them rock bottom as Brighton run out 5-0 winners

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

More misery for Frank Lampard. More gloom. More concern.

Coventry's pointless – and goalless – start to the season extended to four Premier League games and left them rock bottom.

This was a stuffing by a free-scoring Brighton side who had five different players on the scoresheet and ran out easy winners.

Lampard's men showed fight and created some decent first-half opportunities and that should not be overlooked.

Yet classy strikes from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouye, Lewis Dunk and Yasin Ayari, and a Pascal Gross penalty, underlined the Seagulls' superiority.

Coventry had Taiwo Awoniyi deservedly sent off early in the second half and Brighton, already 2-0 up, took them to the cleaners.

There was more gloom and misery for Frank Lampard as their pointless - and goalless - start to the season rumbled on

Lampard agony continues

When Lampard guided Coventry to promotion as Championship title winners last term, romance in the game breathed.

Here was one of the greatest players of his generation returning one of English football's traditional old clubs back to the big time after a traumatic 25-year absence.

Lampard rates the success as the finest achievement of a managerial career which has not always reached the heights he hit as a player.

The greater challenge, of course, will be keeping the Midlands outfit in the big time.

The 48-year-old spent £130million in the summer but the effects of that lavish spree have yet to be felt.

On this evidence, Coventry's survival chances are slipping and wealthy owner Doug King watched on from the stands here.

That Hull and Ipswich already have two wins apiece will merely add to his concerns.

But Sky Blues fans sang their hearts out until the death here and Lampard will need that support if he is to turn the situation around.

Coventry cannot score

Brighton, typically, popped the ball around with a swagger early on but Coventry gradually steadied themselves and fashioned some decent opportunities.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS COVENTRY (3-4-2-1): Rushworth 6; Amenda 6, Thomas 5.5, Pinnock 6; van Ewijk 6, Onyeka 6 (Yirenkyi 73, 6), Grimes 6 (Torp 84), Dasilva 6.5; Rudoni 6.5 (Thomas-Asante 73, 6), Mason-Clark 6 (Cherif 60, 6); Awoniyi 5.5 Sent off: Awoniyi 53 Manager: Frank Lampard 5.5 BRIGHTON (4-2-3-1): VERBRUGGEN 8, Kadioglu 6, Vuskovic 6 (Struijk 78), Dunk 7.5, Boscagli 6 (Osman 78); Gross 7, Ayari 7; Gomez 6.5 (Costinha 84), Yalcouye 7 (Chema Andres 65, 6), Du Cuyper 6.5; Kostoulas 7.5 (O'Riley 84) Scorers: Kostoulas 35, Yalcouyé 51, Gross 70 (pen), Dunk 83, Ayari 90 Manager: Fabian Hurzeler 7.5 Referee: Tony Harrington 6.5 Attendance: 31,492

Jay Dasilva was a threat on the left flank and his dangerous cross was met by Jack Rudoni, whose right-foot volley drew the best of Bart Verbruggen's saves.

Brighton's goalkeeper earned the player of the match honours and his side hit Coventry with a vicious sucker-punch in the 39th minute.

Kostoulas showed delightful skill to create the space to drive a low, right-foot shot past Carl Rushworth.

Lampard said: 'We created chances but didn't take them and then we're one-nil down from a moment of quality – welcome to the Premier League.

'Their second goal was the most disappointing because it was a mistake from us and then the red card, at 2-0, makes it very difficult.

'We need to be more clinical to give ourselves a chance in this league and we need to be honest about that. This wasn't a nice feeling.'

Six minutes into the second half, Yalcouye raced behind a leaden-footed defence to coolly slot home the Seagulls' second.

Awoniyi, a £9million summer signing from Nottingham Forest, then saw red for elbowing Maxim De Cuyper and Lampard had no issues with the decision.

The game was already up for his men but Gross added a third from the spot after Bobby Thomas felled Kostoulas.

Remarkably, centre-half and captain Dunk scored with a stupendous 35-yard shot which flew into Rushworth's top corner before Ayari's neat curling effort late on.

Seagulls score again

Lewis Dunk scored the pick of the goals as Brighton became the division's top goalscorers

Having thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 on the opening day, this latest crushing victory maintained Brighton's impressive start to the season.

It remains early days, but Hurzeler's side appear set fair for another year of progress.

It was all too easy in the end but 13 goals from their opening four games makes them the Premier League's current top goalscorers.

Hurzeler said: 'I wouldn't say it was a complete performance, but our goalkeeper was great and we were ruthless in front of goal.

'If you have that desire to score then you can do it from different positions.

'I wasn't surprised by Lewis' goal because he has a great right foot and shows that technique on a daily basis in training.'

Brighton finished eighth last season to qualify for the Europa Conference League and next up is a trip to Manchester United in the Carabao Cup and a home clash with Arsenal.

Hurzeler added: 'We should stay very humble but also have a belief that we can go anywhere and compete.'

Sports.title: Furious Mikel Arteta is beginning to sound a lot like Sir Alex Ferguson after his latest referee outburst - but this is why it could backfire for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Furious Mikel Arteta is beginning to sound a lot like Sir Alex Ferguson after his latest referee outburst - but this is why it could backfire for Arsenal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Three points secured on a gritty night away in Sunderland.

After what happened here last time out for Arsenal in November, Brian Brobbey’s injury-time equaliser halting a five-game winning run, many assumed Mikel Arteta would be chuffed afterwards.

It’s now five wins in a row and, just as crucially, a show of defiance in many ways. Bruno Guimaraes’ stunning strike – including a cupped ear celebration to a club who detest him from his Newcastle days – and David Raya’s world-class save to deny Enzo Le Fee’s spot-kick both typified this.

Yet, Arteta strode into the post-match press conference with steam coming from his ears.

I opened proceedings, asking about John Brooks’ controversial decision to award the Black Cats a penalty on 54 minutes.

Ezri Konsa, who had a tough night at the hands of many wrestling jousts with Brobbey, was embroiled in another such battle – this time with Dan Ballard.

Mikel Arteta was incensed despite Arsenal earning a hard fought 2-0 victory over Sunderland

Arteta claimed the decision to award Sunderland a penalty was 'not acceptable' and compared Dan Ballard's action to a 'judo roll'

David Raya saved the resulting penalty but Arteta hit out at the awarding of the spot-kick post match

Both had hold of each other’s shirts in the area as the ball arrived, Ballard falling to the deck. Brooks’ call for a penalty was very soft, incorrect even, the pair each culpable for the holding.

Le Fee stepped up to take the resulting penalty, which Raya sprang at full stretch to tip onto the right-hand post.

The memory of that save went out of the window initially for Arteta, though, incensed over the decision.

‘(What) we have to go through today in my opinion is not acceptable,’ Arteta fumed.

‘I watched it 20 times, and I cannot find a way to understand how we even think to give a penalty.

'But I'm sad that we have to discuss in such a beautiful game something at this level that has the gravity to change the course of the season, and it can cost you the championship.

'It's a judo roll.’

It was Newcastle away all over again, that night in November 2023 springing to mind. On that occasion, Mikel Arteta described the decision to award Anthony Gordon’s winning goal against Arsenal as ‘disgraceful’ and ‘embarrassing’.

Arteta wants to make sure that the refereeing fraternity are aware that any major decisions which, in his eyes, go incorrectly against Arsenal will be called out

His comments post-match sounded a lot like legendary Man United boss Sir Alex Ferguson

While Arteta was right to be aggrieved over the decision, but needs to be careful as such forthrightness could go against Arsenal if he is seen to be putting undue pressure on referees

Again, walking into the room, the Spaniard was full of anger and you had a sense of the tirade he was about to unfurl.

Rewinding back to Arsenal’s last-gasp escape against West Ham at the end of last season, where the VAR overturned Callum Wilson’s equaliser, Arteta had said he now ‘realised how difficult and how big the referee’s job is’.

He had forgotten about this when it came to Brooks’ judgement. There was an element of Sir Alex Ferguson about his words. Winning wasn’t enough. He wants to make sure that the refereeing fraternity are aware that any major decisions which, in his eyes, go incorrectly against Arsenal will be called out.

A further line channelled his inner Ferguson.

‘I cannot find an explanation, honestly. That's why I'm going to try to find an explanation now,’ he said.

The Spaniard was right to be aggrieved over the decision, but needs to be careful. Such forthrightness could go against Arsenal if he is deemed to be putting undue pressure on referees.

On the other side, it also showed the wider mindset at Arsenal. Having tasted a first league title in 22 years, and experiencing such a tight finish last time round, Arteta and Arsenal are not leaving anything to chance.

They know how tight the margins are and want to get ahead of the curve. Making a point about refereeing decisions now is a psychological marker. That can have an effect in the months to come when a tight, game-changing call arises. Every point counts at this level.

On this decision, Arteta was right, Brooks’s call harsh because of the level of contact Ballard and Konsa had placed on each other.

Arsenal, though, do like to get physical in the area so need to be careful themselves going forward.

It remains to be seen what level of restraint Arteta can keep going forward, for he’s on a tightrope.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
