World.title: The final haka: All Blacks’ emotional Baltimore farewell [video]
World.content:
The final Greatest Rivalry Haka was performed in Baltimore. Images via SSRugby

The All Blacks delivered their final Haka in the Greatest Rivalry series at the packed M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, the US.

While the New Zealand national team may have lost the inaugural series, they have shared many memorable moments in South Africa, and amongst their South African rivals and fans.

One includes former AB Ma’a Nonu, now playing for the Sharks, who responded to the team with his own performance, as a gesture of goodwill, respect, and admiration for his country and culture.



GREATEST RIVALRY’S FINAL HAKA

With All Blacks captain Ardie Savea ruled out through injury, Codie Taylor captained New Zealand in Baltimore against the Springboks squad.

The Haka was led by the 35-year-old, who performed the Kapa o Pango version of the ceremonial song and dance.

Kapa o Pango in Baltimore 😤🇳🇿



The All Blacks are looking to end the series on a high 🔥



📺 Stream #RugbysGreatestRivalry on DStv: https://t.co/0P0NNhnwKw pic.twitter.com/tC6CztDZ6d — SuperSport Rugby (@SSRugby) September 12, 2026

It was a particularly touching scene, given that the All Blacks played the Springboks in the US for the first time.

The New Zealand team has performed the Haka eight times during the series, before each Springbok test match and four provincial matches against the Sharks, Bulls, Lions and Stormers.

After the final whistle blew in Baltimore, signalling South Africa’s 43-28 victory, the All Blacks linked arms with the Boks as they joined their rivals for their own match tradition, kneeling in prayer after each game.



WHAT IS THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE ALL BLACKS PERFORMANCE?

The Haka – which involves chanting, movement, facial expressions and rhythmic stamping – dates back centuries as a traditional Māori ceremonial performance used to welcome guests, celebrate achievements, mourn loved ones, and show strength and unity.

The All Blacks first performed it during their historic 1905 British tour.

The Kapa o Panga version was developed specifically for the national team, signifying their “pride, unity, and purpose.” It was first performed by player-turned-assistant coach Tana Umaga against the Springboks in 2005 in Dunedin

While the Haka is Māori in origin, it can be performed by New Zealanders of different ethnic backgrounds, particularly in sporting teams and schools.

For the All Blacks, the squad comprises Māori, Pasifika, European/New Zealand, and other backgrounds. All players participate when the team performs the Haka, although

Māori players may have a particularly personal cultural connection to it.

New players are taught the haka when they join the All Blacks, and the team periodically works with a haka tutor to refine it.

Non-Māori may perform and even lead the song, but are required to educate themselves on its cultural context. The leader of the Haka is known as the kaea and is typically a senior member of the team who commands respect and leadership amongst his peers.

World.title: ‘We need to set up VAR’ – Kaizer Chiefs coach Da Cruz makes PSL plea
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs head coach Fernando Da Cruz has become the latest coach to call for the introduction of VAR in the Premier Soccer League (PSL).

Da Cruz made the call after his side were held to a 1-1 draw by Polokwane City at the old Peter Mokaba Stadium on Saturday.

The result saw Amakhosi drop to fourth place in the Betway Premiership standings, with Chiefs once again left frustrated by controversial refereeing decisions.



Chiefs fitness trainer Julien Le Heran, who also acted as Da Cruz’s translator after the match, revealed that the coach believes VAR would help improve refereeing standards in the PSL.

“He says also just to finish, also to develop the PSL, to help our referees, we need to set up the VAR,” Da Cruz said.

“He says because against Richards Bay, one offside, there was no offside and then we could score goals. Against Siwelele, the goal of [Wandile] Duba was a goal and today there was a penalty.”



Da Cruz acknowledged that VAR can sometimes work against a team, but believes its primary purpose should be to ensure fairness and help officials make the correct decisions.

The French coach also views the introduction of VAR as a worthwhile long-term investment for the league.

“So, he says if we want to continue to develop the championship, we need to set up the VAR to help our referees.



“Sometimes it can be against us, but for three games it can be with us,” he added through his translator.

Da Cruz looking for VAR as Chiefs drop point

Since taking charge of Kaizer Chiefs, Da Cruz has suffered just one defeat, and the Frenchman will now hope his side can turn their impressive start into a sustained title challenge.

Amakhosi will now turn their attention into the Caf Confederation Cup preliminary round.



Do PSL need VAR?

World.title: Sister Bethina turns 20: Behind SA’s unofficial anthem
World.content:
Sister Bethina, the unofficial anthem of the Springboks, blared through the speakers at the M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, where South Africa played their rugby rivals, the All Blacks. The iconic song, recorded by artist Mgarimbe, celebrates its 20th anniversary this year.

The Boks won 43-28 and claimed the inaugural Greatest Rivalry series 3-1.

‘SISTER BETHINA’ ROCKS BALTIMORE

As with every Springboks match, rugby fans watching the match live in the stadium vibed to the sounds of Mgarimbe’s Sister Bethina.



The DJ played the song at the M&T Bank Stadium after the All Blacks wrapped up their performance of the Haka.

Take a look…

WHAT IS THE MEANING BEHIND THE UNOFFICIAL ANTHEM?

Sister Bethina – which was released in 2006 – is named after a fictional character from the SABC 2 series Soul City, played by veteran actress Lillian Dube. According to Mgarimbe, the song was accidentally recorded after a drunken night out.



“I just took the mic and started singing,” he told SA Music Mag.

Over the years, Sister Bethina has been played at various national gatherings. Earlier this month, the song was played when the Springboks took on Australia and New Zealand.

In 2023, Mgarimbe sampled his song on another anthem, Amabokoboko, this time commissioned by SA Rugby.

World.title: Four bodies found in Gqeberha
World.content:
GQBERHA – An investigation team has been established in the Eastern Cape following the gruesome discovery of four bodies in Gqeberha.

Police spokesperson, Colonel Siphokazi Mawisa confirmed the bodies of four male victims aged between 20 and 30, all with gunshot wounds, were discovered at G-West, Walmer.

“The circumstances surrounding the incident form part of the ongoing investigation. In an effort to identify possible witnesses, police conducted enquiries in the surrounding areas with no positive results. No arrest has been made.

“Police are appealing to anyone who may have witnessed anything suspicious or who may have information that could assist the police to come forward. Anyone with information is urged to contact the investigating team leader of the Provincial Serious and Violent crimes Unit (SVCU), Lieutenant Colonel Monde Sithole on 082 457 2812 or the nearest police station or alternatively call SAPS Crime Stop at 08600 10111.”

World.title: Counterfeit goods worth R9m seized in Marabastad
World.content:
MARABASTAD - The SAPS and its crime-fighting partners have seized counterfeit goods worth more than R9million in Marabastad, Gauteng.

More than 10,000 fake items were confiscated during a multidisciplinary operation.

The items include branded sportswear, footwear, cosmetics and cellphone accessories.

The operation forms part of a nationwide crackdown on the illegal trade and distribution of counterfeit goods.

SAPS said counterfeit goods can pose health and safety risks to consumers, while causing financial losses to legitimate businesses and the economy.

World.title: District Six residents demand safety plan
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Representatives of Cape Town's District Six community have demanded better safety and security in the area.

This follows the recent violent protests at a neighbouring Cape Peninsula University of Technology campus which residents say spilled beyond the campus boundaries.

Community representatives have now written to university management requesting an urgent meeting to avoid future disruptions.

The District Six Civic Association wants campus management to meet with them over these issues.

“When CPUT decided to rename its campus to District Six, they need to understand they became a part of an existing community, a community of people where 60 000 plus were forced removed from District Six. You cannot us a name and not take cognizance of what that name holds, you don't own that name, the dynamics are complex,” said District Six Advocacy Committee Chairperson Tania Kleinhans.

Community leaders said they want to work more closely with the campus management to resolve issues.

They also expect feedback from the university when classes resume on Monday.

District Six Working Committee Secretary, Shanaaz Arnold said: “Not all of the students was rioting, so they ones that Jeff encountered was actually running away, trying to hide because some of them were taken out of their dormitories because they did not want to participate, so we really want CPUT to come to the table.”

CPUT spokesperson Lauren Kansley confirmed academic activities resume on Monday.

Kansley said the institution understands the concerns from District Six residents after violent protests spilled beyond the campus.

The University said students involved in illegal protest action face criminal charges and could jeopardise their academic futures.

World.title: Iran's economic ties to Dubai hard to break despite war
World.content:
DUBAI - In the markets of old Dubai, saffron, cumin, pistachios and almonds from Iran still fill the stalls, as if the two shores of the Gulf were not separated by war.

Last month, the United Arab Emirates announced the suspension of trade and financial exchanges with Tehran, which has responded to American attacks by targeting the US-allied country and tightening its grip on the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

But in old Dubai, where Iranian merchants are firmly established, they do not believe there will be a break in the ties forged over decades between the UAE's financial hub and southern Iran.

Since the start of the war, certain Iranian products have become scarcer, and others have seen their prices soar, says Morteza Asaadi, who runs the grocery store his father founded in 1963.

Most traditional foodstuffs, such as nuts or zereshk, small red berries used in Persian cuisine, remain available, however.

"It's just coming. How? I don't know, but it's coming," he said.

Two wholesalers interviewed by AFP on condition of anonymity said they are still sourcing from Iran, notably via Omani ports.

"We can't export from the Emirates anymore, but we can still bring in certain goods," one of them said.

In Yasser's saffron shop, the precious spice arrives by air from Mashhad, in north-eastern Iran, thanks to the resumption of air links after a brief interruption.

- Dubai's Iranian community -

Dubai is home to a large Iranian community, estimated at several hundred thousand people, which has contributed to the emirate's commercial development and weathered the various periods of tension with Tehran.

After the US tightened its sanctions against the Islamic republic in 2012, "those in Dubai managed to convince their partners in Abu Dhabi that the trade, regardless of the sanctions, needed to continue because it was contributing to the UAE economy," Mehran Haghirian of the London-based Bourse & Bazaar Foundation think tank told AFP.

In 2024, the UAE was the main entry point for goods into Iran, accounting for more than 30 percent of imports, worth $21 billion.

World.title: ‘It’s too early to link the killings’ - Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner
World.content:
KEMPTON PARK - Acting Gauteng Police Commissioner Fred Kekana said investigators have found some similarities, but there's no evidence yet that the cases involve one perpetrator.

Four women were found dead, partially clothed, with visible bruising and their bodies were discovered in the same general area around Rhodesfield.

Police have formed a task team to investigate the deaths.

"While there are similarities in some of the circumstances surrounding the cases, it will be premature at this stage to conclude that the four cases are linked or that they involve one perpetrator."

Meanwhile, the family missing Kempton Park runner Elizabeth Moselakgomo is waiting to find out whether an unidentified body found in the area is hers.

Moselakgomo disappeared on Wednesday after going for her usual evening run in Rhodesfield.

Family spokesperson Dawn Gouden asked members of the public not to share unverified information.

“On Saturday the body of an unidentified female was located in the vicinity of York Street. Due to the injuries caused and being late at night the family members of Elizabeth could not identify the body.

“The female's body was later taken to the state mortuary of which on Monday the family of Elizabeth and other family members would proceed to identify the body.

We humbly ask that the public refrain from any unverified and unconfirmed information,” Gouden said.

World.title: Gauteng Transport MEC condemns intimidation in taxi industry
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Gauteng Roads and Transport MEC Kedibone Diale-Tlabela is condemning intimidation, threats and extortion in the taxi industry.

She said there is no place for criminality in Gauteng’s public transport system and is warning that those involved will face the full might of the law.

The department said operating licences could be revoked where unlawful conduct is proven.

The MEC is urging taxi operators to resolve disputes through lawful industry structures.

Diale-Tlabela said government will work with law enforcement to restore stability and accountability.

World.title: Yellow Level 4 warning for WC and NC
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The South African Weather Service has issued a Yellow Level 4 warning for disruptive rain in parts of the Western Cape and Northern Cape.

Rainfall is expected to cause flooding and disruption from this afternoon until tomorrow evening.

A cut-off low-pressure system is also expected to bring scattered to widespread showers and thundershowers, which could affect essential services including water and electricity supplies, as well as schools.

The weather service warns that homes in some communities could be destroyed while bridges, roads and mountain passes may be closed.

World.title: Fourth Kempton Park victim found in sports gear
World.content:
KEMPTON PARK - Police are warning women in and around Kempton Park, particularly the Rhodesfield area, to exercise extreme caution following the discovery of the bodies of four women in the same area over a period of approximately two months.

Police are looking for multiple suspects following the harrowing discovery.

The fourth victim found was allegedly wearing sports gear.

Police spokesperson Brigadier Athlenda Mathe said preliminary information gathered by detectives indicates concerning similarities in the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

“The bodies of the women were found half naked and with visible bruising and the discovery sites are located within the same vicinity.

“While investigations are still underway and SAPS has not, at this stage, confirmed that the deaths are linked to a serial killer, the similarities are sufficiently concerning for the police to issue a public warning and intensify investigations,” Mathe said.

Acting National Police Commissioner, Lieutenant General Puleng Dimpane, has directed the Gauteng Provincial Commissioner to immediately establish a dedicated multidisciplinary task team to investigate these cases and determine whether there are links between the incidents.

“The task team will comprise detectives from specialised units, including the Murder and Robbery Unit and the Investigative Psychology Unit, as well as other relevant disciplines and resources required to urgently advance the investigation.

“SAPS is appealing to anyone who may have information that could assist the investigation, particularly residents, motorists, security personnel and members of the community who may have observed suspicious activity in the Rhodesfield and surrounding areas, to come forward,” Mathe added.

Members of the public with information can contact Warrant Officer Elvis Manyike on 082 465 7249 or provide information anonymously through the MySAPS APP.

World.title: Linda Mwananchi storms Nairobi in bold Sifuna show of strength
World.content:
Linda Mwanachi Presidential candidate Edwin Sifuna,address his supporters on September 13th 2026 at Jacaranda grounds in Nairobi,during Linda Mwanachi rally in City. [Edward Kiplimo,Standard]

Nairobi on Sunday offered the clearest sign yet of Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s bid to emerge as a major opposition force, as the Linda Mwananchi movement turned the capital into a stage for an open challenge to President William Ruto ahead of the 2027 General Election.

From All Saints Cathedral to Jacaranda Grounds, it was a sea of humanity as thousands of supporters followed the Nairobi Senator and his Linda Mwananchi team through the city in a largely peaceful procession, chanting his name and cheering his declaration that he is ready to become Kenya’s sixth President.
