World.title: Red threads, witches and upside-down tortillas: Mexican folk wisdom from our grandparents
World.content:
On Aug. 28, Mexico celebrated Grandparents’ Day, an annual tradition since 1983 that recognizes not only our grandparents’ boundless love, experience and wisdom, but also the invaluable contributions they make to Mexican families and communities.

In a country where many parents and caregivers work, grandparents often play a fundamental role in raising children, including picking them up from school, preparing their meals, and keeping them company or supervising them while their parents are away from the home. In fact, according to the University of Colima’s El Comentario, 30% of children in Mexico are cared for by their grandparents.

While capturing the full scope of their impact is nearly impossible, Mexico News Daily did its best, collecting stories from folks across Mexico about the lessons they learned from their grandparents. Some are amusing and quirky, while others are unexpected and confounding.

No matter their essence, though, each word chronicles the everyday wisdom and legacy of those who have left a deep and abiding impression for generations to come.

Pregnancy and babies

If you are pregnant and there is an eclipse, you must wear a safety pin on your belly to protect the baby.

If a pregnant woman has a craving and does not satisfy it, the baby will be born with the face of whatever she avoided eating.

Newborn babies should wear a red bracelet so that a witch will not suck on them.

Alicantes — a type of snake — hypnotize women who have recently given birth to steal their breast milk.

If a baby has a cough, fever or hiccups, the mother must stick a red thread to the baby’s forehead with saliva so it will go away.

If a baby has droopy cheeks, it is because they were made to sit up too early.

If you shave your baby’s head and rub tomato on it, their hair will grow back curly.

If a pregnant woman’s belly is egg-shaped, she will have a boy; if it is round, she will have a girl.

If you are pregnant and go to the beach, your child may be born with blue eyes.

Food

You should not eat watermelon at night because it bloats the stomach and is hard to digest.

If you do not eat what you are craving, you may get a sore on your tongue.

If you get up from the table before you have finished eating, your mouth may become crooked.

If you do not satisfy a craving, you may develop bile.

If you do not plant with enthusiasm, your harvest will not come in.

You must save the best ears of corn from the harvest to attract abundance.

You must rub the ends of a cucumber to remove “the poison:” meaning, its bitterness.

You should not drink plain water on an empty stomach when you are hungover, because it is harmful.

If you eat tortillas upside down, your insides will turn upside down.

Eat pozole with soda or tea, never with fruit-flavored water.

You have to scold or hit fruit trees so that they bear fruit.

To sleep better, drink warm milk before going to bed.

Witches and witchcraft

If you see red balls in the sky, they are witches . If they look close, the witch is far away; but if they look far away, she is close.

Rub an egg over your body to remove negative energy.

If La Llorona’s crying sounds close, it means she is far away; but if it sounds far away, it means she is close. La Llorona is an old legend about a mother who drowned her children in a river and, in sorrow, spends her nights crying for them. She is particularly associated with rivers, lakes and reservoirs.

Weather

If you bury a knife in the ground, you will prevent it from raining.

You should not bathe after an earthquake because the water has been “shaken.”

If you cross your eyes and a gust of air gets into them, they will stay that way forever.

You should not comb your hair, knit or embroider while it is raining, because lightning could strike you.

The first 12 days of the year predict what the weather will be like in each month: these are the famous cabañuelas .

Illnesses

To cure a sore throat, you have to rub roasted tomato on the chest and the soles of your feet.

To cure a cough, you have to iron some pieces of cloth, place them on the back and chest, and sleep with them warm.

Cold enters through the feet; that is why you should not walk barefoot inside the house.

You have to “cool” your eyes — by putting saliva in them — after watching television ; otherwise, you could go blind.

If you feel empachado — with indigestion or a blocked stomach — someone must massage your belly until that person begins to burp; that will relieve the bloating.

If a dog has a cough, you must put a necklace of limes around its neck so it will go away.

Death

If you are lying down, about to fall asleep, and a friend invites you out, you must say no; otherwise, you may encounter death.

If you hear an owl screeching, it means that someone you know will die.

Other beliefs

To cure espanto — a folk illness associated with fright — you must spit mezcal on the face of the person suffering from it while they sleep.

Espanto is cured by drinking a bitter beverage bought at the apothecary.

You should not buy underwear for your partner because it is bad luck: they might leave.

You should not sweep or do housework at night, because negative energy can enter or money can leave.

If you are going on a trip, you must leave a light on to prevent thieves from breaking in.

Stretching at the table is a way of thanking the devil.

You should not cut your hair after eating because it is harmful.

To make visitors leave soon, you must place a broom upside down behind the door.

Tell us in the comments: Did your grandparents have beliefs similar to these? Which ones do you think are true, and which ones are part of Mexican folklore?

María Ruiz is the Director of Digital Marketing at Mexico News Daily. She enjoys photographing her hometown of San Miguel de Allende in her spare time.

World.title: When Mexico bursts into bloom: A wildflower guide
World.content:
Mexico’s wildflowers astounded me … as if Mother Nature had rolled out the red carpet. Traveling through the central highlands in Querétaro and Guanajuato last September, the roadsides, fields and hillsides were covered in colorful blooms. It was a wow moment. Entire mountainsides shone in a patchwork of vibrant yellows, oranges, reds and pinks. Yet, six months earlier, when I passed through, the same mountainsides were dry, arid and sparse.

However, in September, an entirely different ecosystem lay before my eyes. So much so that I asked the driver to stop along the highway beneath the hillside of Mexican sunflowers. The blooms blanketed the landscape in a cheery yellow; he picked some for me after I shared that I was a botanical artist.

When to see the wildflowers

There are two wildflower seasons in Mexico. The first is in spring, from March to May, when arid regions like Baja California and northern deserts bloom after winter rains. These winter rains cause superblooms where desert plants bloom en masse and carpet the landscape.

The second wildflower season is in autumn, from September to November, after the rainy season throughout Mexico. Native plants put on a brilliant flowering display, bursting into bloom.

Of course, wildflower season may start a little earlier, or end a little later depending on the weather. Having been in Queretàro and Guanajuato in September for the last two years during the autumn wildflower season, I can tell you September is a great time to visit states in Central Mexico.

What flowers can you expect to see?

Cosmos, marigold, Mexican sunflowers, globe mallows, morning glory, salvias, mirasol and many more. From tiny butter daisy flowers blanketing the ground at your feet to the huge blooming shrubs of Mexican sunflowers looking you in the eye. There is a wide variety, from light happy yellows to deep striking purples.

Some flowers were a surprise to me. Like the soft baby pink hues of globe mallows. Not a plant that I had seen before. So, seeing a big patch was quite the sight. Another surprise was massive patches of happy pink cosmos. A popular garden plant, grown for its flowers, it was delightful to find out it is native to Mexico.

Seeing the stunning beauty of wildflowers transform the landscape, I knew there had to be symbolic meanings attached to these flowers.

My top 5

Someone asked me what my favorite flower was. It’s almost impossible to choose, but these five left the biggest impression. Especially the white poppy.

Chicalote, or Mexican white prickly poppy

The Chicalote, a native white prickly poppy, won my heart. Its delicate papery petals shining under the sun were so dreamy and elegant that I painted one. The delicate white petals symbolize tranquility, peaceful dreams and quiet rest.

These white prickly poppy flowers stand for endurance and resilience, peace and sleep.

Because the spiny plant thrives in dry, harsh and disturbed soils where other plants fail, to many it represents the ability to survive tough conditions through deep inner strength.

Mirasol, or cosmos

In a show-stopping display of vibrant pinks, cosmos put on quite a show. Huge patches waved to us along the roadside. Swaying on long feathery stalks as we passed. Another beautiful member of the daisy family, cosmos represents balance, peace and tranquility.

Also, cosmos is believed to act as a bridge between life and the afterlife, linking the physical world with the spiritual realm.

Girasol, or Mexican sunflower

Cherry sunflowers were by far the most common. Entire fields and mountainsides radiated in cheery yellow everywhere I went. This member of the daisy family represents faith, loyalty, and adoration.

Some Indigenous populations associated the flower’s bright face with solar deities. Aztec and Mexica people treated the plant as sacred. Dried sunflower seeds were left as offerings at major ceremonial sites like the Templo Mayor in Mexico City.

Mexican passionflower

Walking the streets of Queretàro, Mexican Passionflowers were abundantly climbing up trees or along old gates. This one was growing outside a church, which I found fitting, as they symbolize the Passion of Christ and the crucifixion.

The 10 petals and sepals represent the faithful apostles, while the corona filaments (seen as the purple inner ring) represent the crown of thorns. Inside, the three stigmas represent the nails, and the five anthers represent Christ’s wounds.

Copper globemallow

New to me, this member of the hibiscus family had me stopping for a closer look. The soft baby pink petals are as delightful as the velvety feel of its leaves. Flourishing in dry, harsh desert heat, the flower symbolizes endurance and resilience. Also standing as powerful emblems of hope, gentle comfort and vitality.

The best way to see them

Take a drive. These flowers line highways and laneways, lowlands and mountain ranges. So, by driving, you will see the greatest variety. I loved them all so much I made a quick sketchbook page with the most abundant. I hope you enjoy them as much as I have over the last couple of years.

Mexico Correspondent for International Living, Bel Woodhouse is an experienced writer, author, photographer and videographer with 500+ articles published both in print and across digital platforms. Living in the Mexican Caribbean for over seven years now, she’s in love with Mexico and has no plans to go anywhere anytime soon.

World.title: From the archive: Are Mexicans really always late?
World.content:
The goal of our “From the Archive” series is to revisit popular stories that capture the unique history and culture of life in Mexico. This Sarah DeVries article — originally published in December 2024 — is a humorous look at a stereotype regarding Mexicans and punctuality.

Before we get into the nuts and bolts regarding Mexican punctuality — or lack thereof — it’s important to clarify one thing. Mexicans are not actually always late.

That said, all stereotypes have to come from somewhere, don’t they? But like everything in life, there’s nuance to it.

Just like people all over the world, there’s room for a great deal of variety. Some people are always on time, and some people never are. Most people are punctual for certain activities, and unpunctual for others.

My dad, for instance, has never been punctual; I remember my mother saying she was terrified he wouldn’t make it to their wedding on time. My ex-husband also has challenges with punctuality, as does one of my best friends; I’ve spent great chunks of my adult life waiting hours.

I’m always super duper on time for everything, though I might let myself get to a party up to an hour late. My kid is leaning unpunctual, but I’m doing my damnedest to lecture it out of her. Because if there’s one thing kids love and respond to, it’s a good lecture.

Linguistic flexibility

One of the problems about even defining “late” is the language around defining time. For a deep dive into this, check out Joseph Sorrentino’s excellent piece on this specific type of vocabulary. Ahorita, al ratito, mañana … None of these words specify an actual time, you see? So “ahorita” could mean right this minute, and it could mean in five hours, or never. Al ratito (in a while) might mean in a couple of hours, or it might mean in a few years, depending on who’s saying it. You get the idea.

And really, this kind of language is useful because it allows for flexibility. In this way at least, Mexico is a flexible country.

Really, it has to be. Things come up that need tending to. Public transportation can be unpredictable. The opportunity to have a meal or talk to a pretty girl might come up. Your mom tells you to go fetch some things from the store, and you don’t tell her, “Sorry, I have plans.” Really, you just never know what can happen!

Life is unpredictable, and Mexicans have a fairly high tolerance for it being unpredictable, which is lucky for all of us.

Sometimes, though, there are things you must be on time for. And a good indicator of what those things are is whether or not there’s a specific time attached to them.

The meaning of ‘tolerancia’

School is one of those things. At my daughter’s school, for example, 8 a.m. is the official time kids have to be in the door. As a courtesy to the perpetually-late parents, there’s a “tolerance” of 10 minutes. To me, this means my daughter must be there before 8 a.m. if we’re not to be seen as rude and irresponsible. To others, it means 8:10 or even 8:11 is the limit. If kids aren’t in by that time, they must wait to enter the 9 a.m. class.

It was like this when I taught school here, too; some things, I suppose, are non-negotiable.

The same goes for official appointment times, even if the official or doctor you’re meeting isn’t exactly on time. So if you have a meeting with, say, immigration, you’d better be there at your appointment time! Some places will let you know that they have a tolerancia (literally, tolerance) of 10-15 minutes. This means that if you’re more than that amount of time late, you lose the appointment!

For other things, usually involving celebrations, arrival and start times are more flexible. This is especially true of parties, to which you can show up rather late without causing a fuss. Unless you’ve promised to bring something essential for the party, they’re just glad to have you there at some point. This doesn’t mean they’ll wait for you to start in on the cake and piñatas, though, so beware!

Clocks vs. cultural norms

Concerts and plays typically start within 15 to 30 minutes of their “official” start time; rock concerts might start hours after they’re meant to. Oh, well!

And if you’re meeting friends, it might depend on the specific circumstances. Are you meeting someone busy who only has a few minutes? Are you meeting them alone? In my group of mom friends, we always know that things can come up. “I’ll text you when I leave” is a good, flexible bridge that keeps people updated but keeps plans flexible.

In my own conservative and somewhat strict view, being on time means showing respect for the other person. If you are not on time, then you do not care about them or their time. And if you are on time, not only are you showing respect for them, but you’re making things easier for yourself, avoiding fluster. My cultural chauvinism is showing, I know.

But for plenty of people here, that’s a ridiculous notion. Why stress so much about being on time when literally anything can happen to make you not on time? Perhaps there’s a message here too about avoiding blame and responsibility. “Se me durmió el gallo” (The rooster went to sleep on me; as in, the rooster didn’t wake me up).

But that’s for another article. For now, I’ll leave you with a cute little proverb, as well as its juxtaposed, more truthful meme:

“Al que madruga, Dios le ayuda.” (The one who rises early receives God’s help.) It rhymes!

“Al que madruga, encuentra todo cerrado.” (The one who rises early finds everything closed.)

Truer words were never spoken.

Sarah DeVries is a writer and translator based in Xalapa, Veracruz. She can be reached through her website, https://sarahedevries.substack.com/

World.title: Mexico’s week in review: Exports and gas production hit record highs as patriotic spirit swells
World.content:
Listen to this article

Bilateral communications were front and center in Mexico the week of Sept. 7, with developments running the gamut from encouraging to combative. U.S. President Donald Trump’s remark that Mexico has “nothing” the United States needs beyond “hot tamales” and “tomatoes” caught fire over the weekend, unleashing a fresh round of provocations from Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio in the days that followed.

Mexico, however, continued to highlight trade and security collaboration with its northern neighbor, though the PISA test results and next year’s midterm elections sparked more conversations at home. Meanwhile, the annual inflation rate ticked up to 3.26% — as expected according to Banxico, which forecasts inflation of 3.5% by the end of 2026. President Claudia Sheinbaum remained optimistic through it all, especially as her administration makes its plans for 2027. Overhead, punishing heat baked Mexico’s northern border states even as monsoon rains drenched the Pacific coast and center of the country.

Didn’t have time to catch this week’s top stories? Here’s what you missed.

2027 budget takes shape

On Monday, Finance Minister Édgar Amador Zamora submitted a 10.6-trillion-peso (US $627.8 billion) budget proposal for 2027 to Congress, an increase of about 1% in real terms over this year. Amador framed the package around “five pillars” — economic growth, protecting government priorities, strengthening revenue, more efficient spending and fiscal discipline. The government is banking on those pillars to shrink the budget deficit to 3.9% of GDP next year from an estimated 4.1% in 2026, even as public debt climbs to 55% of GDP. No new taxes or fuel-price hikes are planned.

Health care gets a 10.9% real-terms boost to 1.1 trillion pesos, largely for IMSS-Bienestar infrastructure and medicine supply, while education rises about 7% to 1.3 trillion pesos to fund new schools. Pension and welfare programs get just over 1 trillion pesos, and debt servicing alone eats up 1.6 trillion pesos — roughly one of every seven pesos the government spends. Security agencies see an 11.6% bump to 331.4 billion pesos, while Pemex funding falls 69.2% as the state oil company pushes toward self-sufficiency.

The National Electoral Institute (INE) is the biggest percentage winner of all, with an 87.5% real-terms increase ahead of 2027 midterm elections, while the Energy Ministry, the National Human Rights Commission and the Federal Electricity Commission absorb the steepest cuts. Sheinbaum said the following day that she is “very satisfied” with the package and that growth could exceed the official forecast of 1.5-2.5%, citing anticipated stability in trade relations with the U.S. and Canada.

Homicides continue to fall

Security officials reported this week that daily homicides fell 53% in August compared to September 2024, the final month of the López Obrador administration, making it the least violent August since 2015.

More than 67,000 people have been arrested for high-impact crimes since Sheinbaum took office, though Security Minister Omar García Harfuch cautioned that “the job is not done.” Days later, from Tuxtla Gutiérrez, the president highlighted a 63% drop in Chiapas’s homicide rate since Gov. Eduardo Ramírez Aguilar took office, alongside nearly 10,000 arrests in the southern state. The same briefing revealed the discovery of a clandestine hospital the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) used to treat injured members.

Olmeca Refinery notches record month

Pemex’s Olmeca Refinery in Tabasco posted its best month yet for fuel production in July, averaging 252,498 barrels per day, a 78.8% jump over June. Gasoline output rose even more sharply, up nearly 128% month-over-month, after equipment fires forced repairs earlier in the year. Despite the milestone, the plant — which began operating approximately two years ago — is still running at roughly two-thirds of its 340,000-bpd capacity.

Fox and PRI’s Alito Moreno join forces

In a striking political reunion, former President Vicente Fox met with PRI leader Alejandro “Alito” Moreno to discuss “the need to build a strong opposition” ahead of 2027 midterms — 26 years after Fox became the first opposition candidate to sweep the once-dominant PRI out of the presidency, and years after he called the party “black vipers, vermin and tadpoles.”

Morena, for its part, dismissed the pairing as “the reorganization of the power elite,” saying in a statement that “they change the names, they invent new organizations, but behind the facade, it’s the same old faces.” The PRI, which ruled Mexico for 71 years, now holds just two of the country’s 32 governorships — the same number as the much smaller Citizens Movement (MC) party.

At her Monday press conference, Sheinbaum branded the reunion “PRIAN” politics dating to the “neoliberal” era of former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, and called Fox a “traitor of democracy” — a jab tied to his role in Mexico’s disputed 2006 election.

Bilateral high points

Trade and security cooperation produced some of the week’s more encouraging bilateral news. Mexico’s exports to the U.S. hit a monthly record in July: US $60.55 billion worth of goods were sent north, pushing Mexico’s share of the $332.92 billion U.S. import market above 18%.

Along the border, Mexican and U.S. forces carried out “High Eagle,” a binational operation to detect and disable drones cartels use to surveil authorities near Tijuana and San Diego. And though bad weather grounded Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s flight to Mexico City on Wednesday, he and Sheinbaum still held a video call on USMCA negotiations that Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard described as “cordial” and “very useful,” with talks on steel, aluminum and automotive tariffs continuing ahead of a fourth bilateral review round.

Bilateral low points

Other exchanges were considerably more combative. Over the weekend, Trump proposed to rename New Mexico “New America,” despite having no legal authority to rename a U.S. state, drawing pushback from the state’s Democratic leaders. Later in the week, from Ecuador, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio doubled down on claims that cartels control “vast territories” of Mexico, hinting the threat may eventually have to be “confronted one way or the other.” Sheinbaum shot back on Thursday morning, telling Rubio to keep Mexico out of U.S. midterm politics and calling his remarks electorally motivated. Rounding out the week, U.S. Vice President JD Vance labeled the Mexican flag “a symbol of the far left” after a protester interrupted his convention speech in Dallas, telling the man to “get your ass over there” if he loved Mexico so much.

Poor PISA scores spark a debate over screens

New results from the OECD’s Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA), given to 7,843 students across 297 Mexican schools, showed that four in 10 15-year-olds — 41.8% — scored below the basic level in science, math and reading, more than double the 19.7% OECD average and Mexico’s worst showing since 2009.

Mexican students averaged 388 points in math, 408 in reading and 414 in science, all well below OECD averages of 463, 461 and 482, and the country has shed seven points in both math and reading since the 2022 test. The decline wasn’t unique to Mexico — the OECD’s education director called it part of a “dramatic” global drop, particularly in reading — and Mexican students still reported unusually high curiosity (80%, versus a 24% global average who called school “a waste of time”). Education International, the global teachers’ federation, pinned the broader slide on shrinking attention spans, heavy AI use and a worldwide teacher shortage. China, Singapore, South Korea, Estonia and Canada topped the rankings.

Education Minister Mario Delgado blamed excessive screen use for the drop in reading comprehension — arguing that “screens make it easy to ‘read’ or consume images” — while defending the New Mexican School curriculum model and promoting traditional games like yo-yos, marbles and spinning tops as a substitute for phone time. He conceded the PISA sample was “statistically representative” even as he questioned whether the test amounts to a comprehensive evaluation of Mexican education. Sheinbaum later told reporters Mexico will roll out new math and reading textbooks next year, including poems and short stories, and push a “return to pencil and paper,” tying the effort to new national guidelines already restricting cellphone use in schools.

Education Ministry, UNESCO team up on AI in schools

Also this week, Mexico’s Education Ministry signed a letter of intent with UNESCO to guide the “responsible” rollout of artificial intelligence in classrooms, with the U.N. body offering technical assistance, teacher training and research support. Officials said the goal is to ensure AI supports, rather than substitutes for, teaching and critical thinking, and the deal also opens the door to new rules on cellphone use in schools.

Mexico prepares for El Grito and Independence Day

With the country’s 216th independence anniversary approaching, more than 18,000 members of Mexico’s armed forces are readying for the Sept. 16 military parade through Mexico City, featuring drones, horses, dogs and a float marking the country’s World Cup hosting duties this past June and July. The holiday kicks off the night before, with Sheinbaum leading the Grito de Independencia from the National Palace balcony and Tejano band Intocable headlining a concert in the Zócalo.

Festivities and gritos will ring out from cities across the country, including in Sinaloa, whose capital city of Culicán will hold a public celebration of Independence Day for the first time in two years.

Points of 🇲🇽 pride

A 20-year-old engineering student from a Chihuahua farming family, Luis Ángel Robles Morales, won a national innovation award for an irrigation filter that is already helping 500 drought-stricken farmers use water more efficiently.

Forward Julián Quiñones and Club América’s Scarlett Camberos earned historic Ballon d’Or nominations, marking the first time two Mexican players — and a Mexican club — have featured on the shortlist for world soccer’s top individual honor.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Gachagua Is Raising Money in America. Kenya’s Law Caps What One Donor Can Give
World.content:
KENYA · POLITICS

Key Facts — The tour A 50-day United States tour that began on 26 August, with stops in five states through early October.

— The party He leads the Democracy for Citizens Party. A court dismissed a petition to cancel its registration this year.

— His own figure Gachagua put the whole election process at 2 billion shillings, about US$15.4 million, in May.

— The single-source cap No one contributor may exceed 20 percent of what a campaign raises.

— The annual cap No contributor may exceed 5 percent of a party’s total yearly expenditure.

— The catch Money from a non-citizen is an offence for the party receiving it, not merely a breach of a limit.

Kenyans abroad may legally fund a party at home. What they may not do is fund it as a bloc, and the ceilings are lower than most reporting of this tour suggests.

Nairobi. Campaign finance rules come from two statutes and a set of regulations gazetted in August 2026. (Photo: “Parliament Buildings, Nairobi, Kenya-21April2010” by Jorge Láscar from Bogotá, Colombia, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0.)

Rigathi Gachagua left Kenya on 26 August 2026 for a tour of the United States lasting about fifty days. His party published the itinerary.

It runs through Spokane and Portland in September, then Kansas, Dallas and Boston into early October. He launched an Oregon chapter of his party in Portland on 12 September.

The first ten days were personal. He said he was taking a break to re-energise and spend time with his wife.

Venues, hosts and participants have not been publicly identified for most of the stops. That absence is worth noting in a tour widely described as a fundraising exercise.

Who He Is Now

Gachagua was impeached as deputy president by the Senate on 17 October 2024. He is not the deputy president, and outlets still using that title are wrong.

He now leads the Democracy for Citizens Party. The High Court dismissed a petition this year seeking to nullify its registration.

He is one of several principals in an opposition grouping. The others include Kalonzo Musyoka, Martha Karua, Eugene Wamalwa, Fred Matiang’i and Justin Muturi.

They signed a pact to back a single candidate and have not named one. A deadline of March 2026 passed, and a retreat in August ended without agreement.

Gachagua now says the choice comes after Christmas. He has said the group will sit down and work on a formula then.

Nairobi. The electoral commission set a presidential campaign spending ceiling of about US$47 million for 2027. (Photo: “A green post box in the central business district of Nairobi” by DesiBoy101, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0.)

The Money, and Who Actually Said What

Reports of this tour have carried large figures. The only budget number on the record from a named person is Gachagua’s own, from 14 May 2026.

He said the whole election process is about 2 billion shillings, roughly US$15.4 million. He said nomination fees would raise half of it and the party would find the rest.

That is a party leader describing his own plan. It is not a commitment by anyone abroad, and it is half rather than the sixty percent that has circulated.

Figures above that have no named source attached. Treat any briefing figure without a briefer as unverified.

What the Law Actually Allows

This is the part that decides how much diaspora money can matter, and it is missing from most coverage. Two statutes and one set of regulations apply.

The Political Parties Act of 2011 lists lawful sources of party funds. It excludes donations from a non-citizen, a foreign government, an intergovernmental body or a non-governmental organisation.

Receiving money from a non-citizen contrary to that section is an offence for the party. It is not a reporting breach, it is a criminal provision.

The same act also caps contributors. No person or organisation may contribute, in any one year, more than five percent of a party’s total expenditure.

The Election Campaign Financing Act of 2013 adds a second ceiling. No contribution from a single source may exceed twenty percent of total contributions received.

Regulations gazetted on 9 August 2026 restate that twenty percent limit. Penalties run to fines of 2 million shillings, about US$15,400, and up to five years.

Why the Distinction Matters

Here is the nuance that changes the story. Kenyans living abroad are citizens, so the non-citizen bar does not catch them and diaspora giving is not unlawful in itself.

What is unlawful is a bloc. A diaspora camp funding a majority of a party budget as one organisation would breach both ceilings at once.

Money from people of Kenyan origin who no longer hold Kenyan citizenship is a different matter again. That is the criminal limb, not the ceiling limb.

So the question is not whether the diaspora may give. It is whether it gives as thousands of individuals under the caps or as one organised source above them.

The Scale the Commission Has Set

The electoral commission gazetted spending limits on 7 August 2026. A presidential campaign may spend up to 6.11 billion shillings, about US$47.2 million.

The combined party ceiling is 24.45 billion shillings, roughly US$188.8 million. Against those figures Gachagua’s stated 2 billion is modest.

The commission itself was reconstituted last year. Its chairman and six commissioners were sworn in on 11 July 2025.

The election falls on Tuesday 10 August 2027. Public officers who intend to run must resign by 9 February 2027.

One Phrase Widely Misdescribed

The word wantam, meaning one term, is not an organisation and nobody runs it. It entered public use in May 2025 at a party rally where Gachagua framed the presidency as a single term.

It then spread well beyond him, into protest, music and online culture. He did not found a movement and he is not being asked to front one.

Any account that describes him as leading it, or as being recruited to lead it, has the sequence wrong. He coined the phrase and it outgrew him.

What Nobody Has Said

There has been no response from the president, the state house or the governing party to this tour or to its fundraising. Nor has the registrar of political parties commented on the caps.

On 4 September the deputy president said the government is not scared of sponsored individuals who think a crowd is votes. He did not mention the tour or the money.

Older attacks from July 2025 are still being recycled as though they were responses to this trip. They concerned a different visit and a different remark, and they are fourteen months old.

Neither has any other opposition principal commented on the idea that donors abroad should have a say in choosing the joint candidate. That silence is the open question of this story.

One further piece of context belongs in any account of the 2027 field. Raila Odinga died on 15 October 2025, and the opposition arithmetic that most readers carry in their heads is out of date.

More: Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can Kenyans abroad fund a political party?

Yes. Kenyan citizens living abroad are citizens, so the bar on non-citizen donations does not catch them.

What are the limits?

No contributor may exceed 5 percent of a party’s annual expenditure, and no single source may exceed 20 percent of a campaign’s total contributions.

What happens if a party takes money from a non-citizen?

It is an offence under the Political Parties Act, not merely a breach of a ceiling.

How much is Gachagua’s campaign budget?

He said in May 2026 that the whole election process is about 2 billion shillings, roughly US$15.4 million.

When is the next election?

Tuesday 10 August 2027. Public officers who want to stand must resign by 9 February 2027.

Sources: Political Parties Act 2011, Election Campaign Financing Act 2013, IEBC Election Campaign Financing Regulations 2026, Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission, Office of the Registrar of Political Parties, Democracy for Citizens Party itinerary.

World.title: São Paulo Cape Town flight: what LATAM’s three weekly nonstops mean for expats in South Africa
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · TRAVEL

Key Facts — What happened LATAM has flown nonstop between São Paulo and Cape Town since 1 July 2026.

— How big Three flights a week run each way, on a Boeing 787-9 widebody jet.

— What it means São Paulo now has two nonstop operators to Cape Town, LATAM and South African Airways.

— The catch Miss a LATAM departure and the next one is two or three days later.

— Who it affects Work travellers, mining and farming staff, split families and tourists in both directions.

— What comes next A May 2026 schedule filing loaded seats on the route through 28 March 2027.

LATAM’s Sao Paulo Cape Town flight has been running since July, three times a week in each direction. Here is how the nonstop works if you live between Brazil and South Africa.

Guarulhos at dusk. The Cape Town flight leaves from here late in the evening and lands in South Africa the next morning. (Photo: “Guarulhos International Airport, São Paulo city, Brazil” by Wilfredor, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.)

The Sao Paulo Cape Town flight has linked Brazil and South Africa since the first of July 2026. It is no longer a launch story, and it is now a settled line in the schedule.

What the route looks like now

LATAM Airlines Brasil opened the route on 1 July 2026. The schedule has it leaving São Paulo late that Wednesday night and reaching Cape Town on the Thursday morning.

The airline uses a Boeing 787-9 on the run. That is a long-range twin-engined jet, the larger of the two Dreamliner passenger models.

Flight LA8060 leaves São Paulo Guarulhos at 22:45 on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. It reaches Cape Town International at 10:55 the following morning.

Flight LA8061 comes back on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays. It leaves Cape Town at 15:50 and arrives at Guarulhos at 19:50 the same evening.

Guarulhos is São Paulo’s main international airport, and airlines code it GRU. Cape Town International carries the code CPT.

What the night flight really asks of you

The outbound leg is a night flight in the strict sense. You board late at night and you land in the middle of the next morning.

Time in the air is about seven hours and ten minutes. The return leg is longer, at about nine hours.

That is short for a crossing between continents. The direct distance is roughly 6,350 kilometres, which is about 3,950 miles.

Seven hours is still not a full night of sleep. Land, shower, eat something and keep your first day in Cape Town gentle.

The flight home to Brazil treats you better. You leave Cape Town after lunch and you are in São Paulo by early evening on the same date.

How the time zones line up

Cape Town runs five hours ahead of São Paulo. Neither city shifts its clocks for daylight saving, so the gap holds all year.

Five hours is mild by long-haul standards. Jet lag on this route is nothing like a trip to Europe or Asia.

That gap also leaves a shared working window. A late-afternoon meeting in Cape Town is still mid-morning in Brazil.

Families split across the two countries feel the same benefit. A Sunday call does not have to wake anybody at four in the morning.

Who actually needs this nonstop

Three groups get the most out of it. The first is people who travel for work between the two countries.

Mining and farming tie Brazil and South Africa together, and staff move both ways. LATAM gives them a second nonstop operator to choose between.

Expat families are the second group. A parent in Cape Town and a child in São Paulo are one flight apart.

Tourists are the third, and they travel both ways. Cape Town and Brazil’s biggest city now have two nonstop operators instead of one.

If you cross once every few years, this changes little. If you cross twice a year, a second nonstop means more dates and more fare options.

What you can reach beyond the two cities

The African side of the network is the best documented part. LATAM widened a codeshare with Airlink, a South African airline, from late May 2026.

A codeshare means one airline sells seats on another airline’s aircraft. Your ticket carries a LATAM flight number, but Airlink flies the plane.

That deal covers 22 routes. From Cape Town it reaches Bloemfontein, George, Kimberley, Port Elizabeth, Upington, Harare and Windhoek.

From Johannesburg it adds Gaborone, Lusaka, Nairobi, Walvis Bay and a long list of smaller South African towns. One booking covers the whole journey, which normally means one check-in.

Reports around the launch also named codeshares with South African Airways and GOL. Neither appears in the schedule filings, and South African Airways is a rival on this route.

What it adds, and what is still unconfirmed

LATAM is not the only nonstop. South African Airways has flown Cape Town to São Paulo since October 2023, and listings still show it twice a week.

Many travellers also route through Doha, Dubai or Addis Ababa, and each of those adds a connection. Fares move with the season, so compare both airlines and your dates.

Return fares were reported from about 10,000 rand (about US$620) in coverage around the launch. That is a report rather than a published tariff, so treat it as indicative.

Currency conversions use the 13 September 2026 rate of 16.14 rand to the US dollar, from open.er-api.com.

Listings show two cabins on the aircraft, economy and business, with no premium economy in between. The cabin is reported as 30 business seats and 270 in economy, which the filings do not confirm.

What to sort out before you book

A May 2026 schedule filing put seats on sale through 28 March 2027. The listing had been pushed back twice, from October 2026 to December 2026 and then to March.

Three flights a week is the number that should shape your planning. Arrive late for LA8061 on a Monday and the next LATAM nonstop is on Thursday.

Build a buffer day into any trip that has a hard deadline at the other end. That is cheaper than a rebooking in peak season.

Check your entry paperwork early, because it is now an online step. Our guide to the South Africa travel permit explains what the electronic authorisation costs and how long it takes.

If the trip is really a move, the numbers matter more than the flight. Our look at the cost of living in Cape Town sets out what a month in the city takes.

How long is the Sao Paulo Cape Town flight?

About seven hours and ten minutes to Cape Town, and about nine hours on the way back.

What days does LATAM fly Sao Paulo to Cape Town?

Departures leave São Paulo at 22:45 on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays. The return leaves Cape Town at 15:50 on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays.

How much is a Sao Paulo Cape Town flight ticket?

Return fares were reported from about 10,000 rand (about US$620) in coverage around the launch. That is a report rather than a published tariff.

Can I connect to other African cities on the same ticket?

Yes. A codeshare with Airlink puts LATAM numbers on 22 routes from Cape Town and Johannesburg, including Windhoek, Harare, Gaborone and Nairobi.

World.title: Kenya Remote Work Permit 2026: What the Official Permit List Actually Says
World.content:
KENYA · VISAS

Key Facts — What happened Kenya’s immigration directorate lists nine permit classes, and none of them covers remote work for a foreign employer.

— How big Class G, the closest fit, needs proof of capital of at least US$100,000 plus a registered Kenyan company.

— What it means Remote workers have no class of their own, so they fall back on business rules or short passes.

— The catch The permit that nomad guides point to does not appear on the directorate’s official class list.

— Who it affects Anyone planning to live in Nairobi or Mombasa while working online for clients or employers abroad.

— What comes next A 90-day window to regularise permits and licences opened on 8 September, officials said.

There is no Kenya remote work permit on the immigration directorate’s published list of classes. Here is what the list does contain, and what you can do with it.

Westlands in Nairobi, where much of the city’s coworking and serviced-flat market sits. What you may legally do from a desk here depends on your permit class. (Photo: “Westlands, Nairobi 2025 14” by Rosiestep, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.)

Search for a Kenya remote work permit and you will find guides naming a class that does not exist. Kenya’s Directorate of Immigration Services publishes nine permit classes, and none of them covers working online for a foreign employer.

What the official list actually contains

The Directorate of Immigration Services is the government body that issues permits and passes. It publishes every class on its own website.

The list runs A, B, C, D, F, G, I, K and M. There is no E, no H, no J, no L and no N.

Class D is employment. Class G is specific trade, business or consultancy.

Class K is for ordinary residents living on a pension or annuity. Class F is specific manufacturing, not a permit for laptop work.

Permits and passes sit under the Kenya Citizenship and Immigration Act of 2011. The directorate names sections 36, 40, 41 and 42 as the legal base.

The class the guides get wrong

Some guides describe Class F as the route for people who work from a laptop. The directorate’s own page says something else entirely.

Its wording is plain. Class F goes to a person who intends to engage, alone or in partnership, in specific manufacturing in Kenya.

Class F also asks for proof of investment funds of at least US$100,000. A foreign salary and a good internet line do not meet that test.

A supposed Class N for remote workers circulates in commercial nomad guides. No Class N appears anywhere on the directorate’s published list of classes.

Searches of the directorate’s own site for remote work and digital nomad return nothing. The tourism ministry’s site and the President’s return nothing for digital nomad either.

Class G, and the wall in front of it

Class G is the closest formal fit for a freelancer or consultant. It covers specific trade, business, consultancy or a profession.

The capital test is what stops most people. The directorate asks for documentary proof of capital to be invested of at least US$100,000.

You also need a registered Kenyan company behind the application. That means a certificate of incorporation, a tax PIN certificate and a shareholders certificate.

Processing costs 20,000 shillings (about US$155), and issuance costs 250,000 shillings (about US$1,930) a year. Currency conversions use the 13 September 2026 rate of 129.45 shillings to the US dollar, from open.er-api.com.

Citizens of East African Community member states pay nothing for either step. The community is the regional bloc that includes Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

The short-term route: the special pass

The special pass is the directorate’s short-stay work document. It lets a foreigner enter and remain for a period not exceeding six months.

Its stated purpose is temporarily conducting business, trade or a profession. That is nearer to consulting work than any permit class on the list.

The fee is US$200 per month on approval for people from outside East Africa. East African Community nationals pay nothing.

The pass needs an organisation behind it. The application form has to be filled, signed and stamped by a company or body.

That single requirement rules out many solo remote workers. Six months is also a visit, not a life in Nairobi.

What a visitor entry does not allow

Most travellers now arrive on an Electronic Travel Authorisation, or eTA. It is an online clearance you must hold before your journey starts.

An eTA is permission to visit, not permission to earn. Kenya‘s Cabinet Secretary for Investments, Trade and Industry made that point again this month.

His ministry said arriving without a visa gives no right to work, trade or run a business. We reported that clarification when it was issued.

Officials warned that breaking the rule can cost a visitor their entry status. The warning named employment, market trading, consultancy and managing a company.

How applications actually work

Every permit and pass application goes through one government portal. It is the electronic Foreign Nationals Services site, known as eFNS.

The portal handles passes, permits, alien cards, permanent residence and citizenship. You can find it at fns.immigration.go.ke.

Payment is by card or mobile money. Immigration offices do not take cash for these applications.

You print the permit or pass from the portal once it has been issued. You then take it to an immigration office for endorsement.

Several class pages require documents in other languages to be translated into English. An embassy, a public notary or a recognised institution has to do the translation.

What a remote worker can realistically do

The nine classes were written for employment, trade and investment. Most people working online for clients abroad fit none of them cleanly.

Class G is the formal route for someone with Kenyan clients and real capital. The special pass is the only short-term work document on the list.

Kenya publishes no rule on visitors who keep earning from clients abroad. That gap is not a permission, and enforcement has tightened this year.

Kenya opened a 90-day window in September for foreign business owners to fix permits and licences. Our guide to that 90-day window sets out what it covers.

None of this is legal advice. Fees and rules change, so read the directorate’s own pages before you pay anyone anything.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Kenya have a digital nomad visa?

No class for remote work appears on the Directorate of Immigration Services list of permits and passes. The nine listed classes cover employment, trade, manufacturing and similar activities.

Is Class F the permit for remote workers in Kenya?

No. The directorate’s page says Class F is for specific manufacturing, and it asks for at least US$100,000 in investment funds.

Can I work online in Kenya on a tourist eTA?

An eTA covers a visit, not work. Kenya’s trade ministry said this month that visa-free or eTA entry gives no right to work, trade or do business.

What does a Kenyan business permit cost?

Class G processing is 20,000 shillings (about US$155) and issuance is 250,000 shillings (about US$1,930) a year. East African Community nationals pay nothing.

World.title: Norse Atlantic Cape Town Flights Restart From London Gatwick for the 2026-27 South Africa Season
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · TRAVEL

Key Facts — What happened Norse Atlantic has resumed its seasonal London Gatwick to Cape Town flights for the 2026-27 southern summer.

— How big Listings show three departures a week now, rising to six a week in October and five over the summer.

— What it means It is the only non-stop link between Cape Town and Gatwick; rivals fly from Heathrow instead.

— The catch No flights are listed after 15 April 2027, so an off-season return needs a different ticket.

— Who it affects Travellers, expats and returning South Africans who book on price rather than on airline.

— What comes next The airline is running a formal process that may end in a sale, merger or partnership.

Norse Atlantic Cape Town flights are running again from London Gatwick for the southern summer. It is a seasonal return rather than a new route, and the schedule listings stop in April 2027.

Cape Town International. The Gatwick service runs only through the southern summer, so the apron looks different in July. (Photo: “Airport apron boarding area at Cape Town International Airport June 2026” by Nick-D, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.)

Norse Atlantic Cape Town flights have started again from London Gatwick for the 2026-27 season. South Africa gets its only direct Gatwick link back, and it is a resumption rather than a new route.

A route that comes back every summer

The Gatwick to Cape Town service is not new. It opened on 28 October 2024 and has run every southern summer since.

Wikipedia’s route table lists it as seasonal, and The South African called it a seasonal service at launch. That single word shapes everything else about the ticket.

The timing is deliberate. South Africa’s summer runs from roughly November to March, which is exactly when northern Europe is cold and dark.

Wesgro’s Cape Town Air Access team helped bring the flights in, The South African reported at launch. Gatwick’s own route development team worked on it too.

If the city is more than a holiday, our guide to the cost of living in Cape Town covers the monthly bills.

What the schedule listings show

Flight listings on FlightConnections, updated on 13 September 2026, show three London departures a week this month. Flight Z0 795 leaves on Sunday, Wednesday and Friday, and Z0 796 flies back.

The service then thickens for the peak. October shows up to six departures a week, November about four, and December to March five.

Every flight is a Boeing 787-9, flown by Norse UK, the airline’s British arm. Only two cabins are sold, Economy and Premium Economy.

The southbound leg is listed at about 11 hours and 30 minutes. The return takes roughly 11 hours and 45 minutes across 5,987 miles (9,635 km).

The last London departure in those listings is 15 April 2027. Nothing at all appears for May 2027 or later.

What the low fare does not include

Norse is a low-cost carrier, and its fares are unbundled. You buy the seat first and add everything else on top.

The South African reported a Cape Town to Gatwick fare of R3,387 (about US$210) one way in October 2024. That was a promotional economy light fare on selected dates, with taxes included.

Currency conversions use the 13 September 2026 rate of 16.14 rand to the US dollar, from open.er-api.com. Season fares move, so treat any headline number as a starting point.

The South African set out the range at launch. Seat-only sits at the bottom, and premium economy includes catering, a larger seat and checked baggage.

That economy light fare carried a cabin bag and a personal item, but no chosen seat and no meal. Change fees and add-on prices only show up during booking, so read the final total.

Gatwick is not Heathrow, and that matters

British Airways and Virgin Atlantic fly between Cape Town and London Heathrow. Norse is the only airline listed on the Gatwick run.

Heathrow is a connecting hub, so an arrival can feed straight into another flight on one ticket. Norse sells its long-haul flights point to point instead.

The South African reported at launch that an easyJet agreement lets passengers carry on across Europe. Wikipedia also lists tie-ups with Norwegian, FlySafair and Aegean Airlines.

That is still not the same as one through-ticket with one airline. Leave a generous gap before anything you have to catch after landing.

The bigger question of who serves Africa’s long-haul routes sits behind all of this. We looked at it in our piece on airlines feeding foreign hubs.

How solid is Norse right now

Norse Atlantic is four years old and still losing money. It reported revenue of US$132 million for the second quarter of 2026.

Its EBITDAR came in at negative US$8.4 million. EBITDAR measures earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortisation and aircraft rent.

Demand was not the problem: the load factor reached 94 percent and unit revenue rose 23 percent. Fuel prices and lower aircraft use still pushed the quarter into a loss.

In July the board turned its strategic review into a formal process. The company said this may result in a sale, merger or partnership.

Norse also cancelled its Los Angeles summer programme this year to protect margins. Routes can be pulled when the numbers stop working.

How to book a route that disappears

Check your return date before you check the price. A seasonal route can look cheap and still leave you stuck outside the season.

No Gatwick departures are listed after 15 April 2027. Last season Norse extended the route into May 2026, so that date can still move.

Do not count on it moving. A delayed move or a June return currently means another airline, and British Airways flies from Heathrow all year.

Buy the bag and the seat when you book if you know you need them. Airport add-ons are the slow and stressful way to do it.

Think harder about travel insurance on a thin seasonal route. With three to five flights a week, the next available seat could be days away.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Gatwick to Cape Town flight a new route?

No. It opened on 28 October 2024 and runs every southern summer, so this is a seasonal restart rather than a launch.

How often does Norse fly from London to Cape Town?

Listings show three a week in September 2026 and up to six in October. From December to March the listings show five a week.

Does the cheapest fare include baggage and meals?

No. Fares are unbundled, and only the premium economy fare was described at launch as including catering, a larger seat and checked baggage.

What if I need to fly back in June or July?

No Gatwick departures are listed after 15 April 2027, although the airline extended last season into May. The Heathrow services are the usual fallback.

World.title: Spring Fiesta Boksburg, South Africa: A 13-Hour Festival on 3 October 2026
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · MUSIC

Key Facts — What happened Soul Candi brings Spring Fiesta back to the Wild Waters Complex in Boksburg on Saturday 3 October 2026.

— How long it runs Gates open at midday and the music runs until 1am, a thirteen-hour day outdoors.

— What it means General access now costs R500 (about US$31) after three cheaper phases sold out.

— The catch No line-up is published on the ticket page, even though tickets are already selling.

— Who it is for Adults only; the organisers bar under-18s, list parking and recommend Uber.

— What comes next Ten of Howler’s nineteen price options were still on sale, including a VIP phase cheaper than the sold-out one.

Spring Fiesta Boksburg runs from midday to 1am on 3 October 2026. Here is what the day costs, how to reach the venue, and what the ticket page still leaves out.

Boksburg on Johannesburg’s east rand. The festival site sits a short drive from here, and most people arrive by car or by Uber. (Photo: “Into Boksburg and ERM” by Part Time Security, via Wikimedia Commons, Public domain.)

Spring Fiesta Boksburg is back on Saturday 3 October 2026, from midday until 1am the next morning. The one-day festival takes over the Wild Waters Complex in Boksburg, east of Johannesburg in South Africa.

What the festival is and who runs it

Spring Fiesta is a one-day music festival put on by Soul Candi. The label started in 2001 as a record shop on Corlett Drive in Johannesburg.

Soul Candi built its name on South African house music. Its own site lists Mi Casa, Euphonik, Cuebur and DJ Fresh among the artists it worked with.

The festival has been at the same venue for years. Organisers called the 2022 edition a delayed tenth anniversary for the brand.

Howler, the ticket platform, has hosted pages for the 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 editions. All four listed the Wild Waters Complex as the venue.

The venue itself is not a concert hall. Wild Waters is a family water park in Boksburg, built in 1984 and normally open by day.

Where Boksburg is and how to reach it

Boksburg sits in the City of Ekurhuleni, the suburban belt east of Johannesburg. The name means place of peace in XiTsonga, and about 3.4 million people live there.

Ekurhuleni is also home to OR Tambo International Airport, the busiest in the country. The airport sits in the Kempton Park area, in the same metro as the venue.

Check the address twice. Howler’s main event page gives Margret Lane, Boksburg, Gauteng 1459, while its pre-registration page lists 1 Margaret Ave, Bardene.

The organisers keep their travel advice short. Parking is available at the venue, and the listing recommends Uber.

Gauteng has a busy spring calendar this year. We also covered the Scorpion Kings at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg on 19 September.

The stage names are unconfirmed, and the line-up is missing

Three stage names circulate for this year: Stay True Sounds, Soul Candi Live and a hip hop floor. None of them appears on the Howler event page, so treat all three as unconfirmed.

The event page carries no line-up at all. Its description is two lines long, giving only the date and the venue.

Past years show what those stage names usually mean. The 2022 page listed a Soul Candi Live main stage and a Stay True Sounds stage hosted by Kid Fonque.

Howler listed that stage in 2022 as hosted by Kid Fonque. Its archived pages name stages rather than artists, so no past bill is quoted here.

The hip hop floor has form too, as a stage called This Is Hi(pH)op ran in 2022 and 2024. Neither that stage nor any artist name appears on the 2026 listing.

What tickets cost right now

Spring Fiesta Boksburg tickets sell through Howler, and the price climbs in phases. Three general access phases have already gone: R250 (about US$15), R300 (about US$19) and R400 (about US$25).

Phase 3 general access costs R500 (about US$31) and was still on sale on 13 September. The cheapest VIP on sale was phase one at R600 (about US$37), with VVIP at R1,650 (about US$102).

Currency conversions use the 13 September 2026 rate of 16.14 rand to the dollar, from open.er-api.com. A booking fee is added at checkout on top of the ticket price.

Hotel bundles and table packages are listed too. The cheapest bundle is R1,350 (about US$84) for two general access tickets and a room.

That bundle includes a shuttle from the Birchwood Hotel, and the listed pickup is midnight. The music runs an hour longer, so late stayers need another way back.

What thirteen hours in the open air asks of you

Gates open at midday and the listing runs to 1am on Sunday. That is thirteen hours outdoors at a water park, not an evening gig.

Howler’s archived pages show shorter nights in 2024 and 2025. Those two listings ended just before midnight and at 11pm.

Boksburg sits on the Highveld, the inland plateau that rises above 1,500 metres. The town itself is at about 1,694 metres, so the sun bites and the night cools fast.

Long-run averages for Johannesburg put October days near 25C (77F) and nights near 12C (54F). October rain averages about 68 millimetres as the summer storm season starts.

Pack for both halves of the day. Sun cover and water for the afternoon, then a jacket for the hours after dark.

Rules at the gate and the ride home

This is an adults-only event. Howler lists no under-18s for 2026, and every past edition on the site carried the same rule.

Earlier editions carried a cashless banner on Howler, but the 2026 page does not. The listing says nothing about how you pay inside the venue.

The event page carries almost no rules text of its own. It links instead to Howler’s ticket refund policy, which is worth reading before you pay.

Sort your ride home before the day starts, not at 1am in a car park. If you are new to the East Rand, a booked hotel nearby is the simple answer.

If you want more live music in Gauteng that month, the season runs deep. Our guide to Joy of Jazz in Sandton covers the last weekend of September.

More: South Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Spring Fiesta 2026?

It runs on Saturday 3 October 2026, from midday until 1am on Sunday morning at the Wild Waters Complex in Boksburg.

How much are tickets for Spring Fiesta Boksburg?

Phase 3 general access is R500 (about US$31) and the cheapest VIP R600 (about US$37). VVIP starts at R1,650 (about US$102), and a booking fee is added at checkout.

Who is playing at Spring Fiesta 2026?

The Howler event page carried no line-up in mid-September. Three stage names circulate, but the organisers have not confirmed any of them.

Where is the Wild Waters Complex in Boksburg?

It is in Boksburg, part of Ekurhuleni, east of Johannesburg and close to OR Tambo International Airport. Parking is available and Uber is recommended.

Sources: Howler, Spring Fiesta 2026 event page; Howler ticket page with all price phases; Howler pages for the 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 editions; Soul Candi; Wild Waters Boksburg; Wikipedia entries for Boksburg, the City of Ekurhuleni and the Highveld; open.er-api.com for the 13 September 2026 exchange rate.

World.title: Tinubu Reaches Paris as His Leave Runs Into the Campaign
World.content:
NIGERIA · POLITICS

Key Facts — Where he is President Bola Tinubu arrived in Paris on Sunday 13 September 2026, continuing a three-week working leave that began in London.

— When it started He left Abuja on 30 August 2026.

— The timing Presidential campaigning formally opened on 19 August, eleven days before he flew out.

— The election Nigeria votes for president and the National Assembly on Saturday 16 January 2027.

— The cost N37.64 billion (about US$28 million) on presidential travel between June 2023 and April 2026, across 52 trips.

— The pattern France is his most-visited country, followed by the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

A three-week leave that starts after the campaign opens and ends four months before the vote is a scheduling decision, not an absence.

Tinubu Reaches Paris as His Leave Runs Into the Campaign

President Bola Tinubu arrived in Paris on Sunday, moving the second half of a three-week working leave to the city he has visited more than any other, four months before Nigerians vote.

The Trip

Tinubu departed Abuja on 30 August 2026 for a three-week annual working leave, with London as the first stop, in an arrangement announced by Bayo Onanuga, special adviser to the president on information and strategy.

He arrived in Paris on Sunday 13 September 2026 and was received by Nigeria’s ambassador to France, Emmanuel Ayodele Oke, in a video posted to the presidency’s official account.

Three weeks from 30 August points to a return around 20 September. The presidency says he will resume official duties that weekend without naming a date.

The Election Is the Context

Presidential campaigning formally opened on 19 August 2026, eleven days before Tinubu flew out. Nigeria votes for president and the National Assembly on Saturday 16 January 2027, with governorship elections on 6 February, under the revised timetable the electoral commission announced on 26 February 2026.

The leave began roughly a week after his party published its presidential campaign council list, naming Tinubu chairman and Vice-President Kashim Shettima vice-chairman. Onanuga said the president would return to join preparations for the January poll.

That sequence is what makes the trip newsworthy rather than routine. A leave taken during a campaign is a statement about how contested the campaign is thought to be.

France is Tinubu’s most-visited country as president.

The Same Cities, Three Years On

Paris was the destination of his first foreign trip as president. He flew out on 22 June 2023 for the Summit for a New Global Financing Pact at the Palais Brongniart, then continued to London on 24 June, reaching Lagos on 27 June and Abuja on 2 July.

This is the same London and Paris sequence, run in reverse. France is his most-visited country as president, followed by the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

What the Travel Has Cost

Presidential travel and related costs came to N37.64 billion, about US$28 million, between June 2023 and April 2026, across 52 trips, according to figures compiled from the government spending platform GovSpend. This is his 52nd foreign trip since taking office.

That averages roughly N1.1 billion, about US$830,000, a month. The naira depreciated sharply across the period, so a single-rate conversion understates the dollar value of the earlier spending.

Annual figures run N9.18 billion in 2023, N25.26 billion in 2024 and N2.7 billion in 2025, with N6.14 billion budgeted for 2026.

Nigeria votes for president on 16 January 2027.

How Much Time Abroad

A tally published on 31 May 2026, marking the administration’s third anniversary, put Tinubu and Vice-President Shettima’s combined time abroad at 344 days across more than 75 trips to 37 countries since 29 May 2023.

Tinubu alone accounted for 261 days and 51 trips, across at least 30 countries. Those are the figures for the administration to date rather than a claim about any single period.

What to Watch

The return date is the first thing. A president who resumes duties on 20 September has four months of campaign before the vote; one who extends has fewer.

The second is whether the travel becomes a campaign issue. Opposition figures have used the spending figures before, and a leave taken after the campaign opened gives them a sharper version of the same argument.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is Tinubu?

He arrived in Paris on Sunday 13 September 2026, continuing a three-week working leave that began in London.

When did the leave start?

He left Abuja on 30 August 2026.

When does Nigeria vote?

Saturday 16 January 2027 for president and the National Assembly; 6 February for governorships.

What has presidential travel cost?

N37.64 billion, about US$28 million, between June 2023 and April 2026 across 52 trips.

When does he return?

Three weeks from 30 August points to around 20 September. The presidency has not named a date.

Sources: State House Nigeria, ThisDay, Vanguard, Pulse Nigeria, INEC, Business Insider Africa.

World.title: TCL Sues Samsung Over False Advertising on Mini LED Televisions
World.content:
TECHNOLOGY · DISPLAYS

Key Facts — The suit TCL North America sued Samsung Electronics America on Monday 31 August 2026.

— Where The United States District Court for the Central District of California, in Los Angeles.

— The models Samsung’s 2026 M Model televisions: the M70H, M80H and M90H.

— The allegation That the sets lack full-array local dimming, relying on edge lighting and software dimming, while being marketed as Mini LED.

— The claims Federal Lanham Act plus California false-advertising and unfair-competition law. Injunction and unspecified damages sought.

— Samsung’s position It stands fully behind the quality and accuracy of its product descriptions.

The argument is not whether the televisions are good. It is whether a backlight that dims in software can be sold under a name that describes hardware.

TCL Sues Samsung Over False Advertising on Mini LED Televisions

TCL North America has sued Samsung Electronics America in a California federal court, alleging that three of Samsung’s 2026 televisions are marketed as Mini LED sets without the backlight hardware the term implies.

What Was Filed

The complaint was filed on Monday 31 August 2026 in the United States District Court for the Central District of California, in Los Angeles. Counsel is the firm Larson LLP.

The claims are brought under the federal Lanham Act and under California false-advertising and unfair-competition law. TCL seeks an injunction and unspecified monetary damages.

The plaintiff is TCL North America, headquartered in Irvine, California, the American arm of China’s TCL Technology. The defendant is Samsung Electronics America, the United States subsidiary of the Korean group.

The Technical Allegation

The televisions at issue are Samsung’s 2026 M Model sets: the M70H, M80H and M90H.

TCL’s specific complaint is that these sets lack full-array local dimming, relying instead on edge lighting and software-based dimming, while Samsung markets them using the phrase Supreme Mini LED Dimming.

The distinction is real and consequential for picture quality. Mini LED as the industry has used the term describes thousands of small backlight elements behind the panel, individually dimmable in zones. An edge-lit panel has its lights along the border and simulates zone control in processing.

Mini LED commands a price premium over conventional LED.

Why the Term Is Worth Fighting Over

Mini LED has become the label consumers use to identify a premium backlight without paying organic-LED prices, and it commands a price premium over conventional LED sets.

If the term can be applied to an edge-lit panel with software dimming, it stops functioning as a specification and becomes a marketing category. That is the outcome a manufacturer investing in the hardware has the strongest reason to resist.

TCL’s own genuine Mini LED line, the QM range, is the product the disputed Samsung sets would be competing against on shelf.

What Samsung Says

Samsung Electronics America has said it stands fully behind the quality and accuracy of its product descriptions.

It is worth noting that the two companies have litigated in the other direction as well: Samsung prevailed in a German case against TCL over what it characterised as fake quantum dot televisions. Neither company comes to this dispute with clean hands on advertising claims.

Chinese manufacturers have taken share in the premium television segment.

The Market Behind the Case

TCL claims it overtook Samsung in United States Mini LED sales between 2023 and 2025. Independent data does not fully support the framing: Counterpoint Research indicates that both TCL and Hisense passed Samsung in the Mini LED segment in 2024.

The broader pattern is the same either way. Chinese manufacturers have taken share in the premium television segment that Samsung and LG dominated for a decade, competing on specification at lower prices, and the specification is what this case is about.

What Would Settle It

A false-advertising claim of this kind usually turns on whether the term has an established meaning in the trade and whether consumers rely on it. Both are evidentiary questions, answered by surveys and industry testimony rather than by teardowns alone.

An injunction would be the outcome with consequences beyond the parties, because it would fix what Mini LED may describe for everyone selling into the United States.
