World.title: Iraq signs deal with Chevron to provide consultancy to BOC
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry signed a deal with Chevron on Sunday to provide technical consultancy services to the Basra Oil Company (BOC).

The deal signed under the auspices of Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair covers consultancies by Chevron during the negotiation period with BOC about the development of the West Qurna-2 oil field, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Oil Ministry.

In early July, the Iraqi cabinet authorized the state-owned BOC to sign a preliminary agreement and non-disclosure agreement with a consortium of US-based Capital TI and Chevron, as well as Qatar’s UCC, to construct strategic oil pipelines.

The consortium will carry out technical and financial feasibility studies to compare routes, including Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan and Basra-Haditha-Baniyas, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Iraqi Oil Ministry signed in February two agreements with Chevron to manage and develop major hydrocarbon resources in the country.

Under the first agreement, Chevron acquired Russia-based Lukoil’s share in Iraq’s West Qurna-2 oil field, one of the biggest oil resources in both the country and the world.

Chevron and Iraq’s Dhi Qar Oil Company and North Oil Company (NOC) have inked a second deal to develop the Nasiriyah oil field, four exploration blocks in the southern Iraqi province of Dhi Qar, and the Balad oil field in Salah al-Din province.

The goal of the negotiations between Chevron and the Iraqi Oil Ministry is to improve the conditions of the contract, specifically with regard to profit margins, revenue-sharing arrangements, capital spending caps, and increased operational flexibility.

Chevron reiterated its commitment to expanding long-term partnerships with the Iraqi government to effectively develop oilfields in the country.

World.title: Iraqi airstrike destroys ISIS hideout in Diyala
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Security Media Cell (ISMC) revealed on Saturday that Iraqi fighter jets destroyed a hideout used by ISIS terrorists in the eastern Iraqi province of Diyala.

The ISMC said in a statement that a precise airstrike was carried out by F-16 fighter jets with two missiles targeting an ISIS hideout in the Narin area in Diyala, resulting in its destruction.

In late July, the Iraqi military announced that security forces had identified and destroyed six suspected hideouts belonging to ISIS in the northern province of Kirkuk during an air operation.

Iraq’s Joint Operations Command said in a statement that an airborne group of Special Forces carried out a rapid security operation, destroying the hideouts in the Zghitun Valley area in precise airstrikes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Iraq, Iran discuss measures after attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein held a phone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqhchi to discuss regional developments and the latest measures following the drone attack on Saudi Arabia.

The two ministers discussed Iraqi decisions to close certain border crossings, as well as the attack targeting Saudi Arabia and the work of the joint investigation committee.

According to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry, Hussein and Araqchi emphasized that addressing the region’s crises, including the situation in Yemen, must be achieved through dialogue, negotiations, and de-escalation of tensions to preserve security and stability.

The two sides discussed the upcoming meeting in Oman regarding the Strait of Hormuz, which will include the eight neighboring countries, the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), Iraq, and Iran.

The discussion comes after the Iraqi authorities announced on Saturday the closure of several border crossings as part of security measures and to investigate violations that occurred there.

The development also comes a day after Baghdad confirmed that the attacks targeting Saudi Arabia originated from a location within the province of Maysan in southern Iraq.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered the formation of an investigative committee to look into the activities of Maysan Operations Command.

Al-Zaidi also ordered the dismissal of the operations commander, the provincial police chief, and the directors of the security agencies, as well as their referral for investigation, following confirmation that the attacks on Saudi Arabia originated from the province.

Baghdad also announced its agreement to Tehran’s request for a joint investigation into the discovery of drone launchers near the border with Iran.

On Friday, Saudi Arabia announced that the East-West pipeline in Riyadh and Medina had been targeted by drones launched from Iraq, resulting in casualties and some damage. The Saudi Ministry of Energy subsequently shut down the pipeline as a precautionary measure.

The Saudi Foreign Ministry confirmed that, at the request of the Iraqi prime minister, Saudi Arabia has chosen not to respond at this time. Instead, it will allow the Iraqi government to take necessary measures to prevent attacks originating from its territory.

However, Saudi Arabia reserves the right to take all necessary actions to protect its sovereignty and security.

World.title: Iraq seizes drone launchers near Iran to stop attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security forces have discovered drone launchers near the border with Iran, two Iraqi security sources told AFP on Saturday.

The development took place after a drone attack targeted a pipeline in Saudi Arabia, which Riyadh and Baghdad said was launched from Iraqi territory.

“Iraqi security forces found drone launchers near the Iraqi-Iranian border in the remote al-Tayeb area of ​​the southern province of Maysan,” a security source said. A second source confirmed these details.

Earlier on Saturday, Iraq decided to close its land borders with Iran and suspend flights to the country, following Saudi Arabia’s announcement that attacks on its territory originated from Iraq.

A source at Basra International Airport said that all flights to and from Iran had been suspended until further notice.

An immediate directive was issued by the General Command of the Iraqi Armed Forces to close the Shalamcheh border crossing in the southern Iraqi province of Basra and evacuate all staff, suspending the movement of travelers and goods until further notice.

Instructions were issued for similar measures at border crossings in the provinces of Maysan, Wasit, and Diyala.

Other border crossings with Iran remained open in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah, which are controlled by the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) in northern Iraq.

The decision did not include a complete closure of the Iraqi-Iranian border but rather was limited to specific border crossings as part of the security measures taken following the attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The land crossings between Iraq and Iran represent vital economic and social arteries. Their role is not limited to the movement of travelers; large quantities of goods, foodstuffs, industrial products, and building materials pass through them, in addition to the movement of pilgrims, especially during religious seasons.

Saudi Arabia announced on Friday that the East-West pipeline had been targeted by several drones launched from Iraq, resulting in injuries to workers.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered an investigation into the Maysan Operations Command and relieved its commander, Jalil al-Sharifi, of his post after it was confirmed that the attacks originated from there.

World.title: Iraq leads OPEC+’s output growth in August
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq led the increase in OPEC+ oil production in August 2026 on a monthly basis by 297,000 barrels per day.

The OPEC monthly report, released on Thursday, showed that the alliance’s production increased to 38.055 million barrels per day in August, compared to 37.757 million in July.

OPEC production increased by approximately 346,000 barrels per day last month, reaching a total of 24.081 million barrels per day, compared to 23.735 million in July 2026.

Saudi Arabia and six other OPEC+ countries decided to maintain their oil production policy unchanged through October 2026.

The seven countries successfully eliminated voluntary production cuts of 2.2 million barrels per day in September 2025 and then 1.65 million barrels per day in September 2026.

In addition to these voluntary cuts, the OPEC+ coalition has been implementing production cuts of two million barrels per day since November 2022, with plans to continue until the end of 2026.

Iraq’s crude oil production rose by about 664,000 barrels per day (bpd) in August, reaching a total of 3.378 million bpd.

Kazakhstan’s crude oil production rose by 159,000 barrels per day in August, bringing the total to 1.807 million barrels per day.

The UAE increased its oil production by approximately 54,000 barrels per day, reaching 3.835 million bpd.

The UAE’s data remains part of the OPEC report despite its withdrawal, as its membership officially continues until the end of 2026, according to internal regulations.

World.title: Iraq unveils solar-powered green taxi initiative to drive EV transition
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministries of Environment and Transport have initiated joint planning sessions to advance the rollout of electric vehicles across the country, formulating the initial framework for a pilot project designated as the Green Taxi.

The initiative focuses on the establishment of dedicated solar-powered charging plazas, designed specifically to decouple vehicle charging from the overburdened national electricity grid, curb operating expenses, and slash automotive emissions as part of a wider state policy to gradually introduce clean energy technologies into the public transport network.

Haider Al-Darraji, Director of the Carbon Economics Company under the Ministry of Environment, stated in remarks carried by the official state newspaper that the project constitutes the initial phase of a systematic national transition toward establishing the pillars of a green economy.

Al-Darraji stressed that any long-term mandate requiring the complete replacement of conventional combustion vehicles must be managed through calculated, progressive regulatory frameworks, ensuring that the ecological transition does not impose undue financial strain on private taxi operators or everyday commuters.

The scope and velocity of subsequent expansion phases will depend entirely on empirical evaluations collected throughout the initial rollout. Authorities plan to measure performance benchmarks, including the actual volume of electric vehicles deployed, operational utilization rates, grid independence, maintenance overheads, driver feedback, and verified reductions in both fuel consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

These real-world data points will serve as the technical blueprint for drafting a broader national substitution program to phase out fossil-fuel taxis over the coming years.

Parallel consultations between the two ministries have also explored practical infrastructure adaptations across existing transport hubs. Abbas Imran Mousa, Director General of the Planning and Follow-up Department at the Ministry of Transport, confirmed that discussions are underway to utilize parking garages and terminals operated by the General Company for Private Transport Administration.

Under this framework, designated public transport bays will be retrofitted with solar-powered charging infrastructure, ensuring that clean mobility solutions can operate autonomously while firmly embedding sustainable transport infrastructure across the country.

World.title: Iraq needs over 10,000 new schools to end overcrowding, report warns
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq requires more than 10,000 new school buildings to effectively eliminate severe classroom overcrowding and cultivate a modern pedagogical environment, according to a report released on Sunday, September 13, 2026, by the economic monitor Eco Iraq.

Despite the country maintaining an operational footprint of more than 40,000 schools serving primary and secondary pupils nationwide, the observatory underscored that existing facilities remain entirely inadequate to absorb the country’s expanding student population.

The monitor highlighted that structural deficits continue to constrain daily operations across the public education system, noting that at least 8,000 new school facilities are immediately required simply to phase out multi-shift schooling and transition toward a single-shift model where each school administration operates an independent building.

Achieving an optimal learning setting free of excessive classroom density pushes that requirement well past the 10,000-facility threshold, reflecting decades of demographic growth outpacing physical infrastructure construction.

The report also drew attention to persistent disparities in building standards across rural and peripheral regions, confirming that around 200 mud-brick schools and roughly 800 caravan-style temporary classrooms remain in active use, primarily clustered across Salah al-Din and Dhi Qar governorates.

The observatory concluded by calling on the Ministry of Education to adopt decisive capital allocation programs, emphasizing that high-density demographic hubs—most critically Baghdad, Mosul, Basra, and Dhi Qar—must sit at the very top of federal school-building initiatives to dismantle the ongoing educational backlog.

World.title: US dollar reaches 157,000 IQD in Baghdad and Basra on Sunday
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Parallel market exchange rates for the U.S. dollar climbed further across Iraq’s primary commercial centers on Sunday, September 13, 2026, with selling rates touching the 157,000-dinar threshold in both Baghdad and Basra.

The latest market bulletin highlights an expanding premium over the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory peg of 131,000 dinars per $100, reflecting persistent cash demand across wholesale trading floors and merchant counters.

In Baghdad, wholesale and retail bureaus quoted the greenback at a selling price of 157,000 dinars against a buying rate of 156,500 dinars for every $100, extending Saturday’s upward momentum with a tight 500-dinar margin.

The southern trading hub of Basra matched the capital’s figures precisely, recording identical selling rates of 157,000 dinars and buying prices of 156,500 dinars as merchant demand held firm across the southern commercial axis.

In the northern market of Erbil, dollar valuations advanced in close synchrony, settling just slightly below the central and southern exchanges. Bureaus across the regional capital posted selling prices of 156,750 dinars per $100, alongside a buying rate of 156,500 dinars, underscoring tight trading spreads and steady liquidity flows across all three regional markets as the business week gathered pace.

World.title: Decade on, disability policy rejig in limbo
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ten years after the current disability law was passed, govt is yet to frame a revised National Policy for Persons with Disabilities. The existing National Policy for Persons with Disabilities was adopted 20 years ago.

"This prolonged delay is particularly concerning because a contemporary national policy is essential to translate the rights guaranteed under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPDA) Act, 2016 and India's commitments under UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities into a coordinated, measurable and adequately resourced whole-of-govt framework," stated the organisation, Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change (DwDAoC), in its letter to the minister for social justice and empowerment and secretary of Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD).

Govt had acknowledged the need for a new national policy in its 2022 public notice inviting comments on the draft policy. The task force constituted to draft the policy had submitted the draft on Oct 12, 2021, and the deadline for stakeholder comments was Sept 30, 2022. Four years after the consultation process, India continues to operate under the national policy formulated in 2006, pointed out the letter.

When drafting the new policy, the department explicitly acknowledged the significant developments since 2006, including India's ratification of the UN convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, enactment of RPDA, 2016, and adoption of National Education Policy, 2020.





In 2016, RPDA replaced Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995. "As an organisation led by and representing health professionals with disabilities, we are particularly concerned about the gaps that arise when disability policy is not effectively integrated across health, social protection and other sectors. The medicalisation of disability in professional assessment and eligibility has also been challenged .

.. These judgments underscore the need to move decisively towards a rights-based, functional and accommodation-oriented approach rather than one that treats disability itself as a proxy for incapacity," stated DwDAoC founder Dr Satendra Singh in his letter.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The letter pointed out several shortcomings in the draft national policy including the lack of adequate convergence with health ministry's proposed accessibility standards for healthcare and how accessibility requirements for goods and services remained inadequately reflected in public procurement frameworks.

The organisation sought the current status of the revised national policy, reasons for its delay, whether a revised draft had been prepared following consultations, the proposed mechanism and timeline for further consultation, if any, and the expected date by which the revised national policy would be notified.

World.title: Murder accused takes out 'victory march' after bail, SC tells Haryana cops to produce him in court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Taking a stern view of a murder accused taking out a "victory procession" on being granted bail by Punjab and Haryana HC, Supreme Court has directed Haryana Police to produce him before it.

A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta also recorded in its order that despite a non-bailable warrant being issued against the accused, he had not been produced in custody.

The matter was taken up for hearing on Sept 8.

Taking note of the counsel's submission that the accused, Vishal, had held a procession after getting bail and threatened witnesses, the bench directed the accused to surrender. "We will hear you once you surrender and then seek bail.

Taking out a victory procession on bail is not right," it said.

It noted that the non-bailable arrest warrant issued in Aug has not been executed and the accused has not been arrested by the police. It added that the warrant could not be executed for reasons which the court was not going into at present.

"However, we direct the superintendent of police, district Charkhi Dadri, Haryana to ensure that the warrant is executed and respondent is produced before this court on the next date, which is being fixed as Sept 21, 2026," SC ordered.





It directed the registry to forward a copy of the order to the SP within 24 hours.

The high court granted bail to the accused in the murder case on April 23.

An altercation took place between the accused and family members of the complainant, Rajbala, on Oct 27, 2022 after Vishal allegedly started constructing tin sheds on a disputed plot of land. During a heated exchange, Vishal allegedly hit several people with lathi and axe, grievously injuring several persons belonging to the complainant's side, one of whom died.

World.title: For governance draft, MHA asks Ladakh bodies to answer 7 queries
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Ladakh outfits in talks with the home ministry on safeguards for the Union territory (UT) have been asked to submit a draft proposal addressing seven questions on the larger governance structure for Ladakh, including the division of powers and functions between the proposed UT-level body and the seven district councils.Sources involved in the dialogue process between the Union ministry of home affairs (MHA) and Ladakh administration and Leh Apex Body (LAB), Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) and activist Sonam Wangchuk, told TOI that the Sept 9 round saw a presentation by MHA on the three-tier structure: the apex UT-level body, autonomous district councils and panchayats.The first question sought suggestions on the name of the UT-level body and its executive arm. A key issue was representation of Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC) members in the UT-level body. The Ladakh representatives were asked if they favoured direct elections to the UT-level body or indirect elections by LAHDCs. A consensus emerged in favour of direct elections.As for the district councils, they will also have direct elections, as per the process already followed for the existing two councils in Ladakh and Kargil.The third question focused on functions to be exercised by the UT-level body "in the interest of uniformity, coordinated development and effective administration". They were also asked what functions should be performed at the district level and what principles should guide allocation of powers between the UT-level body and LAHDCs.Another poser related to subjects in the law-making domain of UT-level elected body.The Ladakh bodies were told to submit answers to the seven queries so that a draft proposal could be prepared for the next round of discussions in Oct.Despite progress on Sept 9, LAB, KDA and Wangchuk expressed disappointment with the lack of "headway" in the discussions a day later. When contacted, Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra disagreed and said the talks were productive."Clarity was offered on the proposed constitutional safeguards. Besides, an assurance was given to the Ladakh bodies that their demand for withdrawal of cases related to the violent events of Sept 24, 2025, as well as compensation would be put up before the Ladakh lieutenant governor," said Kundra.While all other Ladakh representatives sounded positive, Wangchuk demanded that no major decisions on the proposed powers of the UT-level body be made till it is in place.

World.title: A diary full of engagements, and the hard task of reconciling conflicting stands
World.content:
New Delhi: PM Modi keeps a rather busy schedule at global events and it was no different as New Delhi hosted the Brics summit, with his schedule chock-a-block as he held 15 sit-down bilateral and numerous pull-aside meetings over three days since Friday.

And, it was not only about numbers, but also India's success in having the grouping of 11 countries, some of whom like Iran and the UAE having deeply adversarial positions on the West Asia conflict, to sign on to a joint declaration affirmed.

PM had the hard task of reconciling the conflicting takes of different countries - some like Russia and Iran are avowedly anti-West and some others, including India, do not want Brics to be pitted as a counteract against the West, and the wordings of joint declaration served the Indian interest well.

World.title: Xi proposes 5-point initiative, calls for 'larger integrated market'
World.content:
New Delhi: Chinese President Xi Jinping Sunday proposed a five-point action plan, including an "open source and inclusive AI" initiative, along with digital industry and trade and investment facilitation as he urged Brics members to cooperate for a stable supply chain and a large integrated market.

Also, urging Brics to rally the Global South and act as an active, stabilising and positive force amid changes not witnessed in a century, he said a world without rules is like a crossroads without traffic lights, where chaos and disorder are all but guaranteed.

"President Xi stressed that Global South countries should jointly defend the rule of law in international affairs, safeguard the basic norms of international relations, including sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and ensure that international law and international rules are applied to all, free from double standards," said a statement issued by Chinese foreign ministry after his address at the second session of the Brics conference.

Xi pushes Chinaâs AI vision of open-source community

Global South countries should hold high the banner of multilateralism, uphold the authority and role of the UN, support multilateral institutions in advancing reform and increasing efficiency, and see to it that reform of WTO proceeds in the right direction. The international financial architecture must be reformed and improved to increase the representation and voice of developing countries,â it said.

Citing the current volatility in a multipolar world, Xi said, âTo bring stability to the world and make it a better place, Brics countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilising and positive force in international affairs, and advance the well-being of all humanity.â





He then went on to elaborate on his economic agenda, arguing cooperation among members of the 11-nation bloc must be strengthened.

As part of the AI initiative, Xi suggested China establish a Brics AI open source community, support cooperation in developing and applying large language models and build an open ecosystem.

In an effort to cultivate new drivers of economic and trade cooperation, China will hold the Brics Forum on Trade in Services next year,â he said on the trade and investment facilitation initiative.

Besides, Xi offered his countryâs assistance in building smart factories and developing standards and norms, with China looking to set up an engineer cultivation alliance for joint development of engineers and mutual recognition of competency standards.

World.title: Fighting in Yemen intensifies, Houthis launch more attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
The conflict in Yemen intensified on Sunday (September 13, 2026), as government forces launched attacks against Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea and Houthis fired into neighbouring Saudi Arabia, which supports Yemen's government.

The Yemeni government vowed to send more forces to the Red Sea coast after conceding a “painful” defeat last week when Houthis captured the port city of Mokha and an island on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a crucial shipping alternative to the Strait of Hormuz.

The escalation — especially Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and its shipping in the Red Sea — adds pressure on global oil supplies and prices, and that could give Iran leverage in its war with the United States.

As Yemen risks descending into another civil war, the United Nations estimated that more than 80,000 people in the impoverished country have been displaced by the fighting since the start of September.

One woman said a mortar shell fell nearby as she fled in the middle of the night from the town of Khawkha in Hodeida province along the Red Sea, shortly before it was captured by Houthis.

“I saw with my own eyes cars and buses burning, and bodies of children and women were lying on the road in a horrific scene,” said the woman, who spoke on condition of anonymity out of concern for her and her family's safety.

Saudi authorities sounded sirens Sunday afternoon (September 13, 2026) in the southern city of Abha and Khamis Mushait province, warning residents to take shelter from potential incoming fire. Both areas were repeatedly attacked by the Houthi in recent weeks.

The Houthis claimed to have used drones and missiles to target Saudi Arabia, including a military base just over the border with Yemen. Houthi military spokesperson Brig Gen Yahya Saree didn't provide evidence or say when the attack occurred.

The Saudi civil defence overnight said a projectile fell in a different area near the border with Yemen along the Red Sea, injuring two people and damaging a mosque and several other buildings. The statement blamed the Houthis.

Saudi Arabia did not announce any new attacks targeting the Houthis.

The Houthis are targeting Saudi oil infrastructure and shipping as part of a recently declared blockade. While the Houthis have said they do not intend to threaten other countries' commercial shipping, markets remain wary and oil prices have risen again.

The National Resistance, a government-allied force that had controlled coastal areas, said more than 500 government fighters were killed on the west coast over the past four weeks — its first comprehensive toll. It said about 1,500 others had been wounded in the fighting since Aug 9.

Its statement said more than 1,000 Houthis had been killed in Hodeida and Taiz provinces. A spokesman for the Houthis didn't respond to a request for comment.

Yemen is home to over 40 million people who fear a return to the civil war that killed 150,000 and brought many others to the brink of famine in one of the world's most sprawling humanitarian crises.

Yemen's internationally recognised government and Saudi Arabia have been battling the Houthis for 12 years. A ceasefire that began in 2022 had mostly halted the fighting.

A senior government official in Yemen said its forces will return to the Red Sea coast and fight back. People fleeing the Houthi advance told The Associated Press they saw forces withdrawing and urging people to run.

Sultan al-Arada, a member of the ruling presidential council, described the collapse of government forces in the port city of Mokha and elsewhere on Yemen's west coast as “painful and regrettable”.

Mr. Al-Arada said in the televised interview aired late Saturday (September 12, 2026) that forces “are currently regrouping and will return to the battle in one form or another.”

On Sunday (September 13, 2026), the Yemeni military said it launched airstrikes on Houthi positions in Mokha and the coastal town of Dhubab, and elsewhere in Taiz province.

The rebels also reported strikes by the Saudi-backed forces in the province as well as artillery shelling in the province of Saada, the Houthi stronghold on Yemen's northern borders with Saudi Arabia.

The Houthis' advance puts them just 32 km from the U.S. military base in Djibouti, on the other side of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. It's the main US base in Africa and one of several foreign military bases in Djibouti, including those of China, France and Japan.

The small Horn of Africa nation is already seeing the arrival of displaced Yemenis making the perilous water crossing. More than 2,000 Yemenis have reached Djibouti, the International Organisation for Migration said.

Djibouti's Economy and Finance Minister Ilyas M. Dawaleh, said on X that the country's navy, coast guard and other specialised agencies were conducting rescue operations and providing emergency assistance.

“The displaced people are in a very bad condition,” said Ahmad al-Masawi, the director of the Al Salam camp in the southern port city of Aden, who appealed to international organisations for assistance.

“They left their homes quickly without any clothing or anything. They are crammed in camps, houses and even on roads."
